To: Information Officer <[email redacted]>
Subject: FOI request — Audit Wales: external audit records of council land dealings at Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, 1970–1996



EXTERNAL: This email originated from outside Audit Wales.



Dear Information Officer,



I sent this request earlier today (20 October 2026) to [email redacted]<[email redacted]>, which returned it as undeliverable (address unknown), so I am resending it to the address published on your Freedom of Information page.



This is a request under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and, where they apply, the Environmental Information Regulations 2004. It concerns Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Vale of

Glamorgan: the farm, its woodland beside Leckwith Road, village green

VG41 (registered on 16 June 1970), and the land later developed as Church View Close. The farmhouse was demolished in 1988.



I understand that Audit Wales holds records inherited from the Wales Audit Office and, for Welsh local government, from the District Audit Service and the Audit Commission. I am trying to establish from the records whether the external auditors examined any council dealing with this land and, if so, who examined it, when and with what result.



Please tell me whether Audit Wales holds, and provide, the following for 1970–1996, for the Vale of Glamorgan Borough Council, South Glamorgan County Council, Glamorgan County Council and the district councils that covered Llandough before 1974:

1. any audit report, management letter, public interest report or value-for-money report that mentions Great House Farm, Tŷ Mawr, Church View Close, village green VG41 or land at Leckwith Road, Llandough; 2. any auditor's working papers or correspondence about any acquisition, sale, exchange, lease or registration of land there by any of those councils, including the registration of VG41; 3. any objection by a local government elector, or any question raised at the audit of accounts, about land at Great House Farm, and the auditor's decision on it, with the date and the auditor (by role) who made it; 4. any correspondence between the auditors and HM Land Registry, BP Properties Ltd (company no. 00699446), Western Ground Rents Ltd (company no. 00342092) or Ideal Homes about the land; 5. if records of this kind for the period are no longer held, the retention or disposal schedule that applied, the date of disposal if recorded, and who authorised it, or the repository to which they were transferred.



Please reply within 20 working days, by 17 November 2026. If you hold no information for any part, please say so; if anything is withheld, please give the exemption relied on. If any part cannot be answered as framed, I would be grateful for advice and assistance under section 16.



Please also make sure that no record relating to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr is destroyed while these enquiries are open.



Yours faithfully,



Requester

Subject: Bute X.6(12) — 1877 Bute trustee accounts/receipts and possible Great House Farm / Llandough transaction

Dear Cardiff Central Library Local Studies / Manuscripts Team,

Glamorgan Archives has advised me (email reference 2026/4097b,
received 30 September 2026) that your library holds a Bute collection
containing reference Bute X.6(12), described as “abstracts of payments
and receipts by the trustees of the Marquis of Bute’s properties, 1877
(copy)”. I am writing to establish access to that exact item and to
ask whether related Bute Estate records in the same collection may
assist a targeted historical search.

The property under investigation is Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr,
Llandough-juxta-Penarth, adjoining St Dochdwy’s Church (approx. ST 168
733), Cardiff. Please keep this distinct from the separate Llandough
Farm opposite the hospital, Llandough juxta-Cowbridge, and Llandow.
The historical question is whether surviving estate material in
1876–1878 records a transaction involving Daniel Thomas / D. Thomas
and the Bute Estate or its trustees concerning this particular
farm/defined parcel. That is a research question, not an assertion
that X.6(12) necessarily concerns this property.

Please confirm:
1. whether Bute X.6(12) is still held by Cardiff Central Library, its
full item title/date coverage and any catalogue or manuscript
identifier;
2. whether the item can be inspected or copied, what the
booking/form/fee conditions are, and whether a digital image of the
relevant 1877 entry can be supplied;
3. whether staff can check the entry/index for Daniel Thomas, D.
Thomas, Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, Llandough Limeworks,
quarrying/mineral rights or a dwelling adjoining St Dochdwy’s
churchyard;
4. whether related Bute X.6 account/receipt volumes, estate ledgers,
correspondence, rent/lease records, conveyances or attached maps/plans
survive for 1876–1878 and can be searched; and
5. if no relevant entry is found, which volumes/indexes were checked
and whether there is a reliable route to other Cardiff Library
manuscript registers or a transfer/custody record.

For any possible match, please provide the exact reference, date,
parties as written, property description, amounts/transaction terms if
recorded, acreage/boundaries, and whether a map or plan accompanies
the entry. Please do not infer that a generic “Llandough” entry refers
to this farm without a supporting description.

Thank you for your help. Please direct me to the correct collection
custodian if Bute X.6(12) has moved or is managed elsewhere.

Kind regards,
Requester

Dear Requester,

Thank you for your email of 16 October 2026 which has been passed to me. Many of the links you have embedded into your email are unfortunately inaccessible, so please make any documentation you wish to send to us available in a pdf or word document format.

I note your request that bp entities place a hold on records relating to Great House Farm/Ty Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth for the period 1969 to date, pending consideration of a possible claim.

Having reviewed the position, we are not aware of any outstanding or live cause of action that bp or any related entity would need to answer in relation to this property. The dispute concerning possession of Great House Farm was the subject of litigation between BP Properties Ltd and Mrs Buckler which was determined by the Court of Appeal in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler (1987). That litigation concluded with the Court of Appeal's judgment, and BP Properties Ltd went on to obtain possession of the site, as your own email records.

In the absence of any explanation of what new claim you believe may now arise, or against which legal entity, we are not in a position to understand why a document preservation obligation would exist, and we are therefore not able to confirm that a preservation hold of the kind you describe will be put in place.

If you do believe you have a specific legal claim against any bp related entity, we would invite you to set out the nature of any interest you claim to hold, the basis of any potential claim, including the legal grounds relied upon and the relief sought so that it can be properly considered.

We look forward to hearing from you with the above information.

Yours sincerely,

Jack Sheehy

Dear Information Commissioner's Office,

Complaint under section 50 of the Freedom of Information Act 2000 — Ministry of Justice / HM Courts & Tribunals Service, MoJ ref IR FOI 260813002 (internal review outcome letter of 9 October 2026)

I ask the Commissioner to decide whether the Ministry of Justice dealt with my request in accordance with Part I of the Act.

The request and the dates
- Request (MoJ ref 260813002): recorded information about court proceedings in 1988–1989 (Barry Magistrates' Court and Cardiff) connected with the eviction and demolition at Great House Farm, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Vale of Glamorgan, including (item 7) any retention, destruction, disposal or archive-transfer records for those court files, and (item 8) any file references, case numbers, register entries or archive references, even where the files themselves no longer survive.
- Original response: 12 August 2026, information not held.
- My request for internal review: 13 August 2026. The MoJ extended the review on 9 September 2026.
- Internal review outcome: letter of 9 October 2026, upholding "not held" under section 1(1)(a).

The points I ask the Commissioner to decide
1. Whether the MoJ made adequate searches. The review letter gives no description of any search: no system, no search term, no date range and no record series. Its conclusion rests on what "may have been" done with the records: that they "may have been destroyed or transferred to an approved place of deposit", and that it is "likely" they were disposed of or transferred.
2. Whether items 7 and 8 were considered at all. They ask for administrative records about the files (retention and disposal schedules, destruction or disposal certificates, transfer and accession records, register or index entries), not for the case files. Records of that kind are created when files are destroyed or transferred, and may survive when the files do not. The review does not give a held / not held answer for either item. Without a search for, and an answer on, items 7 and 8, the conclusion that the information is "not held" under section 1(1)(a) has not been reached on an adequate basis.
3. Whether the MoJ met its duty under section 16. The review suggests Glamorgan Archives "may hold" records transferred from HMCTS, but does not say whether any transfer list or accession record shows that court records for these courts and years were in fact transferred, or give any reference.
4. Timeliness of the review: asked on 13 August 2026 and decided on 9 October 2026.

What I ask the Commissioner to require
a. A held / not held answer for each numbered item, in particular items 7 and 8.
b. A description of the searches made for each item (systems, terms, dates and record series, including any destruction registers, transfer lists or court record indexes).
c. If any record was transferred to an archive, the receiving body and the reference.

I can supply copies of the request, both responses and the extension letter on request.

This is a records complaint only. It makes no allegation against any individual.

Kind regards,

Requester

Dear James,

Thank you for your detailed reply of 22 October, and for clarifying that your correspondence of 11 October reflected your assessment of the proposal as submitted, against the Council's Scrutiny work programming principles, rather than a formal decision of a Scrutiny Chair or Committee.

I understand that scrutiny of this topic would not review individual cases or revisit an individual historic planning decision, would not determine private title, and would not replace the statutory information-rights procedures. I also note that final agreement rests with the relevant Scrutiny Committee and Chair, that the Committee does not currently have capacity for another Task and Finish review while it completes its current piece of work, and that a new topic remains subject to the Council's normal work programming process.

On that basis, I wish to pursue a separate, county-wide topic as follows.

Proposed title: Management of, and public access to, historic planning, land-charges and heritage records.

Purpose: To consider whether the Council's arrangements for retaining, transferring, cataloguing, locating and providing access to historic records are clear, effective and appropriately documented. Reliable historic records matter to any resident, landowner or conveyancer tracing the planning and land-charges history of land anywhere in the Vale.

Proposed scope:

1. The policies, responsibilities and procedures for retaining, transferring, disposing of, indexing and retrieving historic records, including records inherited from predecessor authorities at the 1996 local government reorganisation and earlier reorganisations, how those handovers were documented, and records held on paper or in off-site archives.

2. How searches for historic records are carried out and documented, and how missing, incomplete or unlocated files, appendices and supporting material are identified and explained.

3. How requests for access to historic planning, land-charges and heritage information are received, routed, monitored and answered.

4. Whether published procedures, allocation of responsibilities, record-search practices and service standards could be improved.

The Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr) matter is the background to this suggestion, but it is not a request for Scrutiny to determine, review or revisit that case or any other individual case. I note your point that a topic of this kind would not reflect upon or review individual cases, and I am content for the work to proceed entirely at the level of the Council's systems and practices.

The proposed work would concern policy, governance, records management and service delivery. It would not ask Scrutiny to determine property ownership, make findings about individual liability, or decide the merits of a historic planning decision. My outstanding information requests, including the internal review of EIR request 00210772 and the requests concerning the missing planning appendices, will continue separately through the information-rights routes.

If it cannot be scheduled as Task and Finish work at present, could you please advise whether it can be recorded for a future work programme or considered in another proportionate scrutiny format?

I am not asking for any particular outcome to be predetermined; I understand the decision whether to include the topic rests with the relevant Committee and Chair.

Thank you again for clarifying the process. I would be grateful if you could confirm receipt of this email.

1. Nature and purpose of this notice

This is a formal preservation notice concerning documentary material relating to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, adjoining St Dochdwy's, and the subsequent development of the site, including the area now associated with Church View Close.

It is not a claim form, is not service of proceedings, and is not intended to constitute or replace any FOI request, internal review, complaint, subject-access request or other statutory process already made to any recipient.

The purpose of this notice is to require the preservation of potentially relevant material while the documentary history, title chain, registration history, planning history, possession proceedings, demolition and subsequent development are being reconstructed.

A separate first-stage preservation notice has been issued or is being issued to Cadw / Welsh Government FOI, HM Land Registry Wales Office and DPO, Heneb / GGAT HER, RCAHMW, Vale of Glamorgan FOI Unit and DPO, Glamorgan Archives, South Wales Police FOI, The National Archives, the Wales Office FOI team, and the National Library of Wales. Persimmon Homes (Wales) Ltd has received a separate preservation letter.

You are receiving this notice separately because the published documentary record places you, or a predecessor whose records may remain in your custody or control, within the documentary, legal, professional, administrative or development chain concerning this land.

2. Land and documentary scope

Please preserve, and do not destroy, alter, overwrite, discard, transfer out of custody without a recorded handover, or otherwise dispose of, any record within your possession, custody or control relating to the land or matters identified below.

The scope includes, without limitation, originals, copies, working papers, drafts, annotations, plans, photographs, negatives, films, tapes, maps, registers, indexes, correspondence, emails and attachments, electronic files, archived mailboxes, databases, metadata, internal notes, meeting records, instructions, client or matter files, survey material and other associated records.

The material requested includes:

1. Historical ownership, occupation and conveyancing

The 1877 split; the 1916 and 1939 tenancies; the 1938 Bute to Western Ground Rents conveyance; the 1969 Western Ground Rents to BP Pension Trust conveyance; and any plans, schedules, abstracts, searches, correspondence or other documents relied upon in relation to those transactions.

2. Possession proceedings and subsequent litigation

The 1955 High Court and 1962 Cardiff County Court possession orders; the 1974 proceedings; BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2; House of Lords leave papers, including YHL/PO/JO/10/11/2536; and Buckler v United Kingdom (1989), including associated correspondence, instructions, evidence, plans and working papers.

3. Land registration

The first registration of WA231076, including the application dated 30 November 1982; the first registration of WA240304, including the application dated 23 February 1983; subsequent amalgamation, transfer or closure; and every plan, conveyance, abstract, search, application, correspondence trail or professional file relied upon in connection with those registrations or changes.

4. 1988 possession and demolition

The taking of possession on or about 29 November 1988 and the demolition commenced on or about 6 December 1988, including any planning, listed-building, heritage, police, enforcement, media, contractor, survey, photographic or inter-agency liaison material.

5. Planning and subsequent development, 1989–1996

Planning application 89/01396/OUT; reserved matters application 92/00671/RES; conditions 16–18; GGAT / Cotswold Archaeology material; records concerning any section 52, section 106, planning obligation, local land charge or equivalent instrument; and the transfer from BP to Ideal Homes dated 3 December 1993, together with all associated plans, correspondence, approvals, agreements, searches and completion material.

6. Family records

Records concerning Mary Doreen Williams (died 1983) and William Buckler, insofar as those records relate to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, the land described above, its occupation, ownership, possession, disposal, registration, development or demolition.

3. Predecessor and inherited files

Where you hold, or may hold, a file originating with a predecessor, successor, merged practice, affiliated practice, client or other entity, that material is also within scope.

This includes, without limitation, records originating from:

Loosemores of Cardiff; Robbins Olivey & Blake Lapthorn / Blake Morgan; Linklaters & Paines; Debenham Tewson / DTZ / Cushman & Wakefield; Wyn Thomas + Partners; Ideal Homes Wales; BP Properties; BP Pension Trust; Cotswold Archaeological Trust; Cardiff Bay Development Corporation; and South Glamorgan County Council.

The reference to a predecessor file does not assert that you necessarily hold such a file. It identifies material for which a reasonable custody or succession inquiry should be made where applicable.

4. Preservation steps

Please take reasonable steps to prevent the routine destruction, deletion, alteration or overwriting of potentially relevant material, including material held in archived mailboxes, legacy systems, off-site storage, document-management systems, backup repositories and other electronic or physical stores.

Where relevant material has been transferred to another repository, archive, successor organisation or third party, please preserve the information necessary to identify the transfer and its current location, including any accession, file, box, reference or custody details.

Nothing in this notice requires the creation of records that do not exist. The request concerns the preservation of records already held or controlled by you.

5. Purpose and legal position

This notice is not a finding against any recipient, and I am not asking any recipient to determine title or adjudicate the underlying dispute.

The 1987 Court of Appeal judgment is relied upon here only for matters actually determined by that judgment, including the issues concerning possession, limitation and the October 1974 letters. This preservation notice does not treat that judgment as having determined the complete documentary root of title to the farmhouse parcel.

The underlying documentary history, including the relationship between the farmhouse parcel and the agricultural land subsequently dealt with through Western Ground Rents and BP, remains a matter requiring reconstruction from the primary records.

Accordingly, preservation is requested precisely so that the documentary record can be established from the records themselves rather than through assumptions based on later registration, later occupation, later planning treatment or secondary descriptions.

Dear Requester,

Many thanks for your e-mail below.

I note your comments regarding the distinction between the specific circumstances of Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr) and the broader issue you have identified concerning the Council's arrangements for the retention, transfer, accessibility and disclosure of historic planning, land charges and heritage records. I also note your comments regarding the ongoing Environmental Information Regulations review process, which, as you acknowledge, is being pursued through the appropriate information-rights channels.

In relation to the points raised:

1. County-wide and strategic considerations

I acknowledge your view that the wider issue of how historic planning, land charges and heritage records are managed and made available is capable of being distinguished from the individual circumstances of any single site and may have broader relevance across the county. The decision not to progress the proposed Task and Finish review related to the proposal as submitted and reflected the assessment that the matters raised were closely connected to a specific historical planning case and ongoing information-rights processes.

That said, a proposal focusing specifically on the Council's records management arrangements, access to historic planning information, and the handling of requests for such information could represent a broader issue of potential county-wide application and may be considered separately through the Council's Scrutiny work programming process in conjunction with the relevant Scrutiny Chair. However, for clarity sake, this would not reflect upon or review individual cases.

2. Alternative channels

In response to your request for clarification regarding the alternative channels referred to in my previous correspondence:

(a) Missing, incomplete or contradictory planning and heritage records

The appropriate route will depend on the nature of the concern. Matters relating to planning records held by the Council would ordinarily be raised with the relevant service area in the first instance. Requests for recorded information are appropriately pursued through the Environmental Information Regulations or Freedom of Information processes where access to information is sought. Matters concerning records management may also be raised through the Council's corporate complaints process where the complaint relates to service delivery rather than the application of information-rights legislation.

(b) The Council's handling of information requests

Dissatisfaction with the handling of EIR or FOI requests should ordinarily be pursued through the statutory information-rights process, namely an internal review followed, where appropriate, by a complaint to the Information Commissioner's Office. The corporate complaints process would not generally be used to challenge the outcome of an information request or an information-rights decision, as there are separate processes and policies underpinned by different legislation and regulators.

Questions

1. Was the decision of 11 October taken by officers, or by the Chair or Chairs of the relevant Scrutiny Committee? Under which provision of the Council's Constitution or Scrutiny Procedure Rules was it taken?

The correspondence of 11 October reflected my assessment of the proposal against the Council's established Scrutiny work programming principles and was not a formal decision of a Scrutiny Chair or Committee. In undertaking that assessment, I considered whether the proposal met the criteria normally applied when determining potential items for inclusion within a Scrutiny Committee work programme as outlined above. As I'm sure you will appreciate, we receive many correspondence through this channel relating to on-going case work type scenarios and requesting for Scrutiny which is not the appropriate route, it is not reasonably practicable for a Chair to be cited upon the specifics of operational matters which are addressed or resolved by other means.

As the matter had not been referred to a Scrutiny Chair or Committee for determination, no formal decision was taken by a Committee under the Scrutiny Procedure Rules.

2. Will the narrower, county-wide topic be considered as a Scrutiny topic suggestion?

Should you wish to submit a proposal focused specifically on the Council's arrangements for maintaining, managing and providing access to historic planning, land charges and heritage records, that may be considered as a Scrutiny topic suggestion in its own right. However, finally agreement is the responsibility of the Scrutiny Committee and Chair, and it should be noted and to manage expectation, that they currently do not currently have sufficient capacity to undertake another Task and Finish scrutiny as they are currently undertaking another piece of work.

I would be happy to assist in directing such a proposal through the appropriate process. A separate topic suggestion can be submitted via the Council's website as below, but will be subject to the same considerations that have previously been mentioned and subject to agreement by the relevant Committee Chair - https://www.valeofglamorgan.gov.uk/en/our_council/Council-Structure/scrutiny/scrutiny.aspxDemocratic

3. Can a ward member refer the matter as a Councillor Call for Action, and if so, how?

A ward member may request Scrutiny consideration of a matter of local concern. This would normally be pursued through the relevant Scrutiny Committee and Democratic and Scrutiny Services can provide guidance on the process should a ward member wish to pursue that route.

It may be helpful to note that Scrutiny's role is generally to examine policies, services, performance, and matters of wider public interest rather than to investigate or determine individual cases which could be considered a Member's ward work. Consequently, any consideration by Scrutiny would be expected to focus on broader policy, governance, records management or service delivery issues that are currently operational with recommendations for enhancement (and not decisions for clarity sake) rather than the specific circumstances of an individual historic planning case.

4. Does the Council's corporate complaints procedure apply to the handling of records requests, as distinct from the information-rights routes?

As a general principle and set out above, complaints concerning the handling of requests made under the Environmental Information Regulations, Freedom of Information Act or data protection legislation are expected to be addressed through the relevant statutory review and appeal mechanisms, namely an internal review followed, and thereafter, where appropriate, by a complaint to the Information Commissioner's Office. The corporate complaints process would not generally be used to in relation to information requests handling,  the outcome of an information request or an information-rights decision, as there are separate processes and policies underpinned by different legislation and regulations and a separate regulator.

The corporate complaints procedure may, however, be relevant where a complaint concerns wider service standards or administrative matters that fall outside the scope of the statutory information-rights regime. Whether a matter falls within the corporate complaints process will depend on the specific nature of the complaint.

I trust the above clarifies the position.

Kind Regards,
James

Enquiries Service
The National Library of Wales

I am researching the title history of Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Glamorgan, adjoining St Dochdwy’s churchyard (approx. ST 167 733).

Glamorgan Archives (Louise Hunt, ref. 2026/4097, 24 September 2026) has confirmed that the following references are yours, not theirs, and has directed me to you:

1. D153 — Deeds relating to premises in p. Llandough, co. Glam., comprising a dwelling house adjoining the churchyard, 1811 (D153/1–2), and land (D153 onwards, including items sometimes cited as D153/4–8).
2. D219 — Llandough manorial leases and agreements.
3. The main Bute Estate deposit, GB 0210 BUTE (deeds to 1937; Glamorgan / Cardiff rentals).

I do not ask you to adjudicate title. I ask only whether the following instruments exist in your holdings, and for catalogue references, dates, parties, acreages, and whether a plan is attached.

A. The 1877 division
Does the Bute deposit contain a conveyance, agreement, or other instrument of about 1876–1877 by which the Marquess of Bute (or trustees) conveyed or contracted to convey the farmhouse, buildings and about 10 acres adjoining the churchyard at Llandough to Daniel Thomas (or Thomas and another), while retaining about 9 acres of agricultural land to the east?

B. The 1916 agricultural tenancy
Does the deposit contain a yearly agricultural tenancy, or counterpart, of 1916 from the Marquess of Bute to John Williams of Great House Farm, Llandough?
If yes:
- does the parcels clause describe the whole farm, or only the land Bute still owned after 1877?
- is there a plan?
- what acreage is stated?

C. Rentals 1877–1936 for this farm
Do Glamorgan / Cardiff / Llandough rentals in GB 0210 BUTE distinguish, after c.1877, between:
- a house/buildings holding (Thomas / later Williams), and
- a residual Bute field holding later passed to Western Ground Rents in 1938?

D. Anything that would show the two holdings were treated as one unit again before 1938.

Purpose. HM Land Registry first-registered titles WA231076 (30 November 1982) and WA240304 (23 February 1983; later amalgamated). The 1982/83 files treat the land as one farm. The family case is that Parcel A (house and about 10 acres) had already left Bute in 1877 and was not the land let in 1916, so the 1982 merged title cannot be the same unit as the 1916 tenancy. Your deeds and rentals are the estate-side evidence that can confirm or deny that.

I live in Patagonia and cannot visit Aberystwyth in person in the short term. I would be grateful for:
- catalogue references and a short description of any matching items;
- whether copies can be supplied, and the cost;
- if the 1916 tenancy is not in GB 0210 BUTE, any note of where Bute tenancy counterparts after 1910 were deposited.

This is a new enquiry. It is not a repeat of FOI/2026/11. Glamorgan Archives hold the 1938–44 Western Ground Rents plan/rental book (D696) and have already answered on their own Bute material.

If your correspondence relates to an existing case - we will add it to your case and consider it on allocation to a case officer. If you believe we have either failed to take appropriate steps to respond to your data protection complaint, or we do not provide you with information about the progress or outcome of your complaint within the next three months, you may be able to apply to the First-tier Tribunal to require us to respond to your complaint or to provide you with information about its progress. If you want advice urgently, you should telephone our helpline on [phone redacted]. You can find out more about data breach reporting on our website.
Where a significant cyber incident occurs, you may also need to report this to the National Cyber Security Centre (the NCSC). Dear Ms Mccarley,

FOI 1040/26: request for internal review

Thank you for your email of 29 September 2026 and the attached response to FOI 1040/26. The response says, in full, "South Wales Police do not hold this information." Under your Freedom of Information Complaints Procedure, please treat this email as a request for internal review of that response. I am copying it to the review mailbox named in the procedure.

Grounds

1. Adequacy of search. The request (20 August 2026) asked for incident reports, sudden-death reports, referrals to the Coroner, statements and other records about two deaths: William (Billy) Buckler, late of Great House Farm, Llandough, and Mary Doreen Williams (born 10 August 1913; death registered March 1983, South Glamorgan). The response gives no description of what was searched. A one-line "not held" cannot be tested without one. The ICO's approach is that a not-held answer is judged on the balance of probabilities, by reference to the searches actually made.

2. Corrected date. The request gave William Buckler's death as "on or about 29 May 1990", taken from newspaper reports. Since then, in correspondence on FOI 1264/26 (13 and 16 October 2026), I have confirmed that William Beverly Buckler died at Llandough Hospital on 15 May 1992. If the search was limited to 1990, please re-run it for May 1992, and for all name forms (William Beverly Buckler, William, Bill or Billy Buckler). If you consider that part a new request, please register it, give me the reference and the 20 working-day date, and do not treat it as a reason to delay the review of the rest.

3. Timeliness. The request was received on 20 August 2026 (your email of 28 September confirms this). The 20 working-day limit under section 10(1) FOIA fell on 18 September 2026. The response was sent on 29 September 2026, seven working days late. Please record the breach in the review.

4. Duty to advise (section 16 FOIA). If South Wales Police does not hold these records, the response did not say whether they were never created, were destroyed, or were transferred. Nor did it say who might hold them now, for example the Coroner's office or an archive. Section 16 and the Section 45 Code of Practice expect that advice.

What I ask the review to provide

a) the systems, indexes, archives and date ranges searched, and the search terms used, for each of the two deaths;
b) the retention period that applied to sudden-death reports and Coroner referral records from 1983 and 1990–92, and the policy or schedule it comes from;
c) any record of the destruction or disposal of such records, with the date;
d) whether any records of that period were transferred to Glamorgan Archives, the Coroner or any other body, and if so the reference;
e) confirmation that any surviving record within scope will be preserved while this review, FOI 1264/26 (due 9 November 2026) and the internal review 1188/26 of FOI 719/26 (due 26 October 2026) remain open.

Information about people who have died is not personal data under section 3(2) of the Data Protection Act 2018, so section 40 FOIA does not prevent disclosure of anything found.

I would be grateful for the review outcome within 20 working days, by 18 November 2026. If the review upholds the original answer without describing the searches, the next step is a complaint to the Information Commissioner under section 50 FOIA.

Yours sincerely,

                                            Response Date: 21st October 2026

Request

Request for a preservation notice.

Response

The Freedom of Information Act 2000 creates a statutory right of access to recorded information held by public
authorities. When processing requests for information under the Freedom of Information Act, public authorities have
two duties to consider. Section 1(1)(a) is the duty to confirm or deny that the requested information is held, and
Section 1(1)(b) is to the duty to communicate the requested information to the applicant.

Section 8 of the Act is also relevant here, as it outlines the criteria which need to be fulfilled in order for a request to be
deemed ‘valid’ and therefore suitable for processing under the Act.

Section 8(1) of the Act provides:

(1) In this Act any reference to a “request for information” is a reference to such a request which:

(a) is in writing,
(b) states the name of the applicant and an address for correspondence,
(c) describes the information requested.

Section 84 of the Act clarifies that ‘information’ means ‘information recorded in any form’.

Dear Mr Egan,

Thank you for your reply of 20 October and for confirming that I will be given a reasonable opportunity to ask questions and make comments on business specified on the published agenda.

I maintain my objection to the absence of an in-person option for members of the public. With the meeting now two days away, I will join by Zoom using the link sent on 13 October and participate constructively. This is acceptance of the practical arrangements for this meeting, not withdrawal of my objection.

Your reply answers point 5 of my email of 16 October, but leaves points 1–4 unanswered. I restate them below, with one further question about the notice (question 2), and would be grateful for a brief response to each, if possible before Thursday and in any event within 20 working days of this email:

1. Decision: Who decided that the meeting would be held remotely only, and on what date?
2. Notice: Was the agenda or meeting notice sent to me on 13 October subsequently revised? If so, when was it revised, and on what date was the revised notice published on the Council's website and noticeboards?
3. Published arrangements: Please provide a link or copy of the Council's current published arrangements for multi-location meetings, which section 47 of the Local Government and Elections (Wales) Act 2021 requires the Council to make and publish, and identify whether any revision or replacement of those arrangements applies to this meeting.
4. Public access: What consideration was given to residents who wish to observe or participate in person, including whether a physical public venue was considered and, if so, why it was not made available?

I am not suggesting that the legislation guarantees a physical venue for every meeting. My concern is how the decision was made, which published arrangements apply, and how public access was considered in this instance.

If these questions cannot be answered before Thursday, please confirm that they remain outstanding and indicate when I can expect a response, which I would ask to be no later than 20 working days from this email. Please also retain this exchange with the meeting correspondence and identify where any formal decision or resolution concerning the arrangements is recorded.

Arrangements for Thursday's meeting

a) Public participation and Item 10

Please confirm the time limit for Item 4, the procedure for being admitted from the Zoom waiting room and invited to speak, and any separate time limit or procedure for making representations when Item 10 is reached. I intend to make a brief contribution under Item 4 and to address the Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr business under Item 10, in accordance with your confirmation concerning representations on published agenda business.

b) Circulation and retention of the statement

Please circulate my supporting briefing and read-aloud statement to all councillors before the meeting:

- "Meeting briefing" (https://2026-10-22.bucklerfamily.estate/)
- "Read-aloud statement" (https://2026-10-22.bucklerfamily.estate/meeting-script.txt)

Please confirm whether the written statement can be retained with the meeting papers and referred to in the minutes. If the full briefing cannot be circulated before the meeting, I would be grateful if the statement could at least be circulated and the briefing link made available to councillors.

c) The wider context and any future agenda item

I understand that Item 10 covers two specific requests, and that Item 16 concerns correspondence rather than decisions on unlisted business. I am not asking the Council to determine title to the land or to make findings against any person or body.

The wider history, heritage and outstanding records questions may require separate consideration. If these matters cannot properly be addressed under Item 10, please advise whether I should now submit a request for a properly notified item at a future meeting and whether any particular notice, motion or other procedure is required.

Separate information and preservation matters

Separately from the meeting arrangements, please acknowledge receipt of my internal review request of 13 October (the later of my two emails that day, which stands as sent) and my narrower information request of 20 October, and advise the anticipated response date for each. As my request of 21 September concerns land and environmental information, I would ask that the review consider it under the Environmental Information Regulations 2004, which contain no cost limit equivalent to section 12 of the Freedom of Information Act 2000.

I would also welcome confirmation of whether the Council holds planning files, section 52 or section 106 instruments, or related correspondence from 1988–1992 concerning planning references 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES and, if so, whether those records are being retained pending the wider records enquiries.

The wider experience, which I ask to be placed on record before Thursday

I raise the following so that the Council has my concerns in writing ahead of the meeting:

- My first approach to the Council about this matter received the reply of 20 November 2025: "I regret to inform you that we are unable to assist with the matter you raise." From my side, the Council has not engaged with the substance since then, which is why I have had to escalate by formal requests, an internal review and a complaint about the handling of my correspondence.
- When I was told the matter could be raised at a meeting, I was not told where or when that meeting would be held. Only after I asked for those details so that I could attend did the meeting become remote only. I have travelled some 7,000 miles to be present in Llandough for it.
- The Council regularly tells residents on its public social media that it is a community council that is transparent and approachable and that will answer questions. My experience has not matched that, and I ask the Council to explain the difference.
- For my family, raising these matters at all is difficult. Since the demolition of Great House Farm in 1988, we have lived for 38 years largely silent and in fear about it. I have already explained this to you and to councillors. A remote-only meeting, arranged after I asked to attend in person, is not accommodating of that.
- Thursday is my family's opportunity to have these matters recorded. I ask that this message, my briefing and my statement are kept with the meeting papers, so that the minutes can later be compared with the points raised, and any points not reached can be taken forward at a future meeting.

I appreciate that this is shortly before the meeting. Where a substantive answer is not possible before Thursday, a brief acknowledgement identifying what remains outstanding and when it will be addressed (within 20 working days at the latest) would be helpful.

I remain willing to participate constructively and appreciate your assistance in the run-up to the meeting.

Yours sincerely,

Requester

The County Court, Family Court, Court of Protection, and the District Registries of the High Court Records Retention and Disposition Schedule is the document that is used to manage the retention and destruction of records in HMCTS.

1. This schedule covers the court/tribunal records and associated administrative records held in the County Court, the Family Court, the Court of Protection and the District Registries of the High Court. It covers the records that are created and managed in line with Section 8 and Schedule 1, paragraph 4 of the Public Records Act 1958. HMCTS manages these public records on behalf of the Lord Chancellor.

2. It covers the records for the different jurisdictions and courts that sit in county court buildings (County court (civil), Family court, Court of Protection and District Registries of the High Court).

3. The schedule sets out how long these records should be kept (retention) and what should happen to the records when the retention period ends (disposition). It applies to records in all formats including, but not limited to, digital (for example case management systems or emails), paper and audio.

FORMAL PRESERVATION NOTICE
Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth
Titles: WA231076, WA240304, WA513690 and WA735527
Planning references: 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES

URL: greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com

To each recipient separately, in your own capacity as a current or potential holder, custodian or controller of relevant records:

This notice is addressed to each recipient individually. It is not a joint request, and it does not ask any recipient to speak for, investigate on behalf of, or answer in place of any other person or organisation. Each recipient is asked to respond only in respect of records within that recipient's own possession, custody or control, including records inherited from a predecessor organisation or retained on its behalf.

1. Nature and purpose of this notice

This is a formal preservation notice concerning documentary material relating to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, adjoining St Dochdwy's, and the subsequent development of the site, including the area now associated with Church View Close.

It is not a claim form, is not service of proceedings, and is not intended to constitute or replace any FOI request, internal review, complaint, subject-access request or other statutory process already made to any recipient.

The purpose of this notice is to require the preservation of potentially relevant material while the documentary history, title chain, registration history, planning history, possession proceedings, demolition and subsequent development are being reconstructed.

A separate first-stage preservation notice has been issued or is being issued to Cadw / Welsh Government FOI, HM Land Registry Wales Office and DPO, Heneb / GGAT HER, RCAHMW, Vale of Glamorgan FOI Unit and DPO, Glamorgan Archives, South Wales Police FOI, The National Archives, the Wales Office FOI team, and the National Library of Wales. Persimmon Homes (Wales) Ltd has received a separate preservation letter.

You are receiving this notice separately because the published documentary record places you, or a predecessor whose records may remain in your custody or control, within the documentary, legal, professional, administrative or development chain concerning this land.

2. Land and documentary scope

Please preserve, and do not destroy, alter, overwrite, discard, transfer out of custody without a recorded handover, or otherwise dispose of, any record within your possession, custody or control relating to the land or matters identified below.

The scope includes, without limitation, originals, copies, working papers, drafts, annotations, plans, photographs, negatives, films, tapes, maps, registers, indexes, correspondence, emails and attachments, electronic files, archived mailboxes, databases, metadata, internal notes, meeting records, instructions, client or matter files, survey material and other associated records.

The material requested includes:

1. Historical ownership, occupation and conveyancing

The 1877 split; the 1916 and 1939 tenancies; the 1938 Bute to Western Ground Rents conveyance; the 1969 Western Ground Rents to BP Pension Trust conveyance; and any plans, schedules, abstracts, searches, correspondence or other documents relied upon in relation to those transactions.

2. Possession proceedings and subsequent litigation

The 1955 High Court and 1962 Cardiff County Court possession orders; the 1974 proceedings; BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2; House of Lords leave papers, including YHL/PO/JO/10/11/2536; and Buckler v United Kingdom (1989), including associated correspondence, instructions, evidence, plans and working papers.

3. Land registration

The first registration of WA231076, including the application dated 30 November 1982; the first registration of WA240304, including the application dated 23 February 1983; subsequent amalgamation, transfer or closure; and every plan, conveyance, abstract, search, application, correspondence trail or professional file relied upon in connection with those registrations or changes.

4. 1988 possession and demolition

The taking of possession on or about 29 November 1988 and the demolition commenced on or about 6 December 1988, including any planning, listed-building, heritage, police, enforcement, media, contractor, survey, photographic or inter-agency liaison material.

5. Planning and subsequent development, 1989–1996

Planning application 89/01396/OUT; reserved matters application 92/00671/RES; conditions 16–18; GGAT / Cotswold Archaeology material; records concerning any section 52, section 106, planning obligation, local land charge or equivalent instrument; and the transfer from BP to Ideal Homes dated 3 December 1993, together with all associated plans, correspondence, approvals, agreements, searches and completion material.

6. Family records

Records concerning Mary Doreen Williams (died 1983) and William Buckler, insofar as those records relate to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, the land described above, its occupation, ownership, possession, disposal, registration, development or demolition.

3. Predecessor and inherited files

Where you hold, or may hold, a file originating with a predecessor, successor, merged practice, affiliated practice, client or other entity, that material is also within scope.

This includes, without limitation, records originating from:

Loosemores of Cardiff; Robbins Olivey & Blake Lapthorn / Blake Morgan; Linklaters & Paines; Debenham Tewson / DTZ / Cushman & Wakefield; Wyn Thomas + Partners; Ideal Homes Wales; BP Properties; BP Pension Trust; Cotswold Archaeological Trust; Cardiff Bay Development Corporation; and South Glamorgan County Council.

The reference to a predecessor file does not assert that you necessarily hold such a file. It identifies material for which a reasonable custody or succession inquiry should be made where applicable.

4. Preservation steps

Please take reasonable steps to prevent the routine destruction, deletion, alteration or overwriting of potentially relevant material, including material held in archived mailboxes, legacy systems, off-site storage, document-management systems, backup repositories and other electronic or physical stores.

Where relevant material has been transferred to another repository, archive, successor organisation or third party, please preserve the information necessary to identify the transfer and its current location, including any accession, file, box, reference or custody details.

Nothing in this notice requires the creation of records that do not exist. The request concerns the preservation of records already held or controlled by you.

5. Purpose and legal position

This notice is not a finding against any recipient, and I am not asking any recipient to determine title or adjudicate the underlying dispute.

The 1987 Court of Appeal judgment is relied upon here only for matters actually determined by that judgment, including the issues concerning possession, limitation and the October 1974 letters. This preservation notice does not treat that judgment as having determined the complete documentary root of title to the farmhouse parcel.

The underlying documentary history, including the relationship between the farmhouse parcel and the agricultural land subsequently dealt with through Western Ground Rents and BP, remains a matter requiring reconstruction from the primary records.

Accordingly, preservation is requested precisely so that the documentary record can be established from the records themselves rather than through assumptions based on later registration, later occupation, later planning treatment or secondary descriptions.

6. Acknowledgement and identification of records

Please acknowledge receipt of this notice and, in your own capacity, confirm:

(a) the officer, partner, records manager or other person responsible for implementing the preservation hold;

(b) what records within your possession, custody or control you have identified as falling within the scope above; and

(c) where you identify no records within scope, what relevant systems, files, repositories or predecessor records you searched in reaching that conclusion.

A substantive assessment of title is not requested from you. The immediate requirement is preservation and identification of the documentary material you hold.

The public documentary index and developing evidence record is available at:

https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/

Please monitor that site for subsequent identification of documents, references and specific schedules relevant to your organisation's records.

Where a reliable public email address is unavailable, a postal preservation notice will also be sent. For example, a postal notice will follow to Loosemores, Alliance House, 18–19 High Street, Cardiff [postcode redacted].

Nothing in this notice constitutes an abandonment, waiver or limitation of any claim, position or remedy concerning title, registration, concealment, limitation, reopening, rectification or alteration of the register, or any associated matter.

Regards,

Requester

Dear Defra Information Rights team,

This is a request under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and, where
they apply, the Environmental Information Regulations 2004. It
concerns Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Vale of
Glamorgan (then Glamorgan), a farm occupied by my relatives, the
Williams family, and the records of the Ministry of Agriculture and
Fisheries (MAF) and its Glamorgan committees, to which Defra is the
successor. It is separate from my request 2026/1425E, which is on a
different subject. It is linked to my enquiries with The National
Archives, CAS-347296-M0V4Y1 and CAS-344046-K1S1R2.

Western Ground Rents Ltd (company no. 00342092), to which the Bute
Estate conveyed its interest by a conveyance dated 25 December 1938,
obtained a possession order on 4 July 1955. I am trying to establish
from the records how the farm was dealt with between 1936 and 1955,
who took each decision, and on what record.

Please tell me whether Defra holds, and provide, the following for
Great House Farm for 1936–1955:
1. any National Farm Survey or other MAF farm record for the holding,
including the occupier, the owner and the acreage recorded;
2. any record of the Glamorgan War Agricultural Executive Committee
(or its successor, the Glamorgan Agricultural Executive Committee)
about the farm: inspections, gradings, cultivation or other
directions, supervision orders, or any possession, requisition or
termination of tenancy, with the date and the committee or officer (by
role) who made each decision;
3. any application for, or decision on, the Minister's consent to the
operation of a notice to quit the holding (Agricultural Holdings Act
1948), with the date, the decision and who made it;
4. any compensation claim or payment for the land under the
Compensation (Defence) Act 1939 or the Agriculture Acts;
5. any correspondence with Western Ground Rents Ltd, the Bute Estate
or their agents about the farm, or about the possession order of 4
July 1955 and the land it covered.

If records in scope have been transferred to The National Archives
(for example MAF 32, the National Farm Survey, or the MAF 80 series of
committee minutes), please give the reference rather than treating
that part as not held. If any record in scope was destroyed, please
give the retention or disposal schedule that applied and, where
recorded, the date and the authority for its destruction. If any part
is held by the Welsh Government rather than by Defra, please say so.

Please reply within 20 working days, by 17 November 2026. If you hold
no information for any part, please say so; if anything is withheld,
please give the exemption relied on. If any part cannot be answered as
framed, I would be grateful for advice and assistance (section 16
FOIA; regulation 9 EIR).

Please also make sure that no record relating to Great House Farm / Tŷ
Mawr is destroyed while these enquiries are open.

Yours faithfully,

Requester

Dear Persimmon Homes Legal Department,

Church View Close, Llandough (formerly Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr) – title WA231076 (and former title WA240304)

I wrote to you on 27 September 2026 asking that records about this land be preserved. I have received only automatic replies, so I would be grateful if you could confirm that the preservation request has been passed to the right team.

I now write with a short, specific request for records. As I understand it, BP Properties Ltd transferred the land to Ideal Homes in 1993, Church View Close was then built, and Persimmon Homes (Wales) Ltd is now the registered proprietor of WA231076. I am trying to establish, from the records, what was known and decided about the land when it was bought and developed, and by whom.

Please tell me whether Persimmon (including as successor to Ideal Homes Wales) holds any of the following, and provide copies or a description:
1. the 1993 transfer from BP Properties Ltd, its plan, and the contract or conditions of sale, including any warranty, indemnity or condition given by BP about title, occupation, the 1987 Court of Appeal decision in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler, or the demolition of the farmhouse in 1988;
2. the report on title, pre-contract enquiries and requisitions on title (and BP's replies) for the purchase, so far as they mention the occupation of the farmhouse, the 1987 decision or any claim to the land;
3. any title indemnity or defective-title insurance taken out for the purchase or the development, with the date and the risk it covered;
4. the internal approval for the purchase (for example, the land acquisition or board approval), with its date and the role of the person who approved it;
5. any archaeological report or correspondence about the 1994 excavation on the site (published by Holbrook and Thomas in Medieval Archaeology 49, 2005), and any licence or record for the removal, reburial or retention of human remains found during the development, with where they were reinterred or deposited;
6. any planning condition, section 52 or section 106 agreement, or correspondence with the Vale of Glamorgan Council about village green VG41 or the woodland, linked to planning applications 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES;
7. if any of these records have been destroyed or passed to another party (for example, solicitors or a successor company), the date, the retention policy applied and who holds them now.

I understand that Persimmon is not subject to the Freedom of Information Act 2000, so this is a request for your voluntary help; I am not making any allegation against Persimmon. If you hold nothing, a short note saying so would be equally helpful. A reply by 17 November 2026 would be much appreciated.

Yours faithfully,

Requester

Sirs/Madam,

I write concerning the land now comprising Church View Close, Llandough, formerly Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, including title WA231076 and former title WA240304.

Persimmon Homes (Wales) Ltd is the current registered proprietor of WA231076. Persimmon is therefore a present link in the conveyancing chain arising from the registration of this land in BP Properties Ltd's name in 1982–83, BP's subsequent transfer to Ideal Homes in 1993, and the later development history.

I am conducting a documented investigation into the legitimacy of that title chain. This is not a speculative historical enquiry. The issues arise from identified Land Registry, conveyancing, court, planning and public-authority records, and from specific documentary gaps which remain unresolved.

The central issue is the historic identity and ownership of the land.

The evidence presently assembled indicates two historically distinct parcels:

• Parcel A: the farmhouse, garden, buildings, yard and associated woodland, which the Williams family maintains was acquired out of the Bute estate through the Daniel Thomas transaction and subsequently became the family's freehold interest; and

• Parcel B: the eastern agricultural fields, whose subsequent passage from Bute to Western Ground Rents and then to BP is not presently disputed by the family.

The significance of that distinction is that later documents repeatedly use the expression “whole farm”, although the surviving 1939 tenancy plan is understood to show the eastern fields only. The 1938 Bute-to-Western Ground Rents conveyance is therefore a material title-chain question: what estate was actually capable of being conveyed by Bute in 1938, and did that conveyance include Parcel A?

There is further evidence requiring examination of the period from 1949 to 1974, including repeated attempts to characterise Mary's occupation of the farmhouse parcel as tenancy or permission; the loss of the family's title papers in about 1950–52; the 1955 possession order expressed in “whole farm” terms but enforced everywhere except the farmhouse and garden; the separate 1962 possession proceedings concerning the farmhouse and garden; Mary's express assertion of ownership; and the 1974 proceedings, which were adjourned part-heard and were never finally adjudicated on the family's historic ownership claim.

The Court of Appeal's decision in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 subsequently concerned possession, limitation and the legal effect of the October 1974 letters. The judgment records Mary's asserted ownership and the absence of the documents she said supported it. The present investigation therefore distinguishes carefully between what that judgment decided concerning possession and limitation and the separate question of whether the documentary root and extent of WGR/BP's title to Parcel A were ever actually established.

That distinction becomes particularly important in relation to first registration.

HM Land Registry records show BP's first-registration applications for WA231076 and WA240304 in 1982–83. The surviving registration material also identifies a 31 December 1969 conveyance from Western Ground Rents to BP Pension Trust as a root of title, but that conveyance is not presently included in the 30 July 2026 schedule of documents surviving on the relevant first-registration files. The 1975 conveyance and plan, the 1982–83 registration material, the extent of the two titles and their later amalgamation therefore require direct reconciliation against the underlying documentary title.

There is also an unresolved procedural issue concerning notice and opportunity to object during the 1982–83 first-registration process. Mary Williams remained in occupation of the farmhouse. The family evidence recorded on the evidence index is that notification was not received until after her death on 26 March 1983. I am obtaining the primary notice, service, application and registration records to establish exactly what occurred.

The matters under investigation consequently include possible registration mistake, procedural unfairness, material non-disclosure and, depending upon what the primary records establish, possible fraud or deliberate concealment. There are also unresolved public-authority record questions involving HM Land Registry, court administration and other authorities. These are identified as evidential questions, not asserted as established findings against Persimmon or any individual.

Persimmon's position is therefore directly relevant because its present registered title derives from the historic chain now being examined.

Please provide a substantive response to the following:

  1. Title chain: What documentary chain does Persimmon say establishes its predecessor's title to the whole of WA231076, including the farmhouse, garden and associated land now comprising Church View Close?

  2. BP / Ideal Homes due diligence: What title, acquisition and due-diligence documents were supplied to and reviewed by Persimmon in connection with the acquisition from Ideal Homes, including deeds, plans, title abstracts, searches, requisitions, Land Registry correspondence and enquiries concerning the extent of WA231076/WA240304?

  3. Earlier title documents: Does Persimmon hold, or has it ever held, copies of the 1969 WGR-to-BP Pension Trust conveyance, the 1975 BP Pension Trust-to-BP Properties conveyance and plan, the 1982–83 first-registration application/bundle, or documents explaining the inclusion of the farmhouse parcel within the registered extent?

  4. 1996 correspondence: Does Persimmon retain the correspondence from March 1996 with HM Land Registry concerning WA231076, identified in the surviving title chronology as the last dealing on the file? If so, please provide a copy, subject to any properly applicable exemption or privilege.

  5. Parcel A: Has Persimmon ever reviewed the underlying documentary title sufficiently to satisfy itself that the farmhouse/garden parcel was actually comprised in the title acquired by BP, rather than being brought within the registered extent through the later “whole farm” description?

  6. Present position: Having regard to the matters above, does Persimmon maintain that its title to the farmhouse/garden parcel is supported by an identifiable documentary root independent of the possession and limitation history considered in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler?

If Persimmon maintains that the documentary title to Parcel A is established, please identify the instrument or instruments on which that position depends and the land those instruments actually comprise.

I am seeking voluntary or pre-action disclosure of non-privileged material where possible. If any requested document is withheld, please identify the document or category concerned and the basis upon which it is withheld.

Preservation notice

Please treat this correspondence as formal notice to preserve all documents and electronically stored information within Persimmon's possession, custody or control that may be relevant to the title, acquisition, registration, extent, occupation, planning or development of this land.

This includes historical material inherited from BP Properties, Ideal Homes or any other predecessor, together with deeds, conveyances, plans, title abstracts, searches, due-diligence files, acquisition memoranda, legal/property correspondence, Land Registry correspondence, planning records and communications with public authorities.

Please ensure that no routine retention, deletion, destruction, disposal or overwriting process removes potentially relevant material. This preservation request includes electronic files, archived mailboxes and other electronically stored information where applicable.

The public evidence index and supporting record are maintained at:

https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/

Nothing in this correspondence abandons, limits or prejudices any claim concerning title, registration, fraud, deliberate concealment, procedural unfairness, public-authority involvement, limitation, reopening of historic proceedings, rectification/alteration of the register, compensation or reparations. All rights and remedies are expressly reserved.

This correspondence is not a claim form and does not constitute service of proceedings.

Please acknowledge receipt and refer this correspondence to Persimmon's legal/property team. I request a substantive response addressing the questions above.

Yours faithfully,

Requester (Ret'd Sergeant)

Dear Mr Egan,

New, narrower request under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 (and the Environmental Information Regulations 2004 where they apply)

Thank you for your response of 11 October 2026. This is a new, narrower request. It is separate from my request of 13 October for an internal review of that response, and it is not meant to reopen or pre-empt the review.

Your response explained that the cost estimate was driven by the need to search "all minutes of the council and its committees for a period of 14 years", and by the "significant amount of documents on file from the period 2002-2016 where minutes are in documents rather than published on the website or in archives". To keep within the limit, this request does not ask you to search the council's minutes or minute books for any period. It asks only for any file or record the council itself holds that is specifically about the following, concerning Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr and the land beside Leckwith Road, Llandough:

1. village green VG41 beside Leckwith Road: any record of its registration in 1970 (including whether the council, or the parish council before it, applied for or supported the registration, and who signed on its behalf), and any later proposal to extend or alter it;
2. any comment, objection or consultation response by the council on planning applications 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES, and any correspondence about them;
3. any correspondence between the council and the Vale of Glamorgan Council, BP Properties Ltd or its agents, or the developers of Church View Close about Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr;
4. where the council's own records from before 2002 are now held (for example, which archive, under what reference, and when they were deposited), and any record of the destruction or disposal of council files on the matters in items 1 to 3, with the date and who authorised it.

If you consider that any item would still exceed the cost limit, please tell me which, and I will narrow it further (section 16). If the council holds nothing for an item, please say so. If any records are held by someone else, please say where.

MP Doughty,

Further to the correspondence from Mr Iain Banfield, and my earlier email, I am writing again to be sure, placed on record, is the central issue which HM Land Registry's response still does not answer.

I appreciate that HM Land Registry is not a court and that it cannot simply reopen a Court of Appeal judgment. That, however, does not answer the separate question of whether the land registered in 1982/83 was correctly identified and supported by the documentary title then placed before the Registrar.

Mr Banfield's response relies heavily upon BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2. That judgment post-dated the registration by approximately four years. It records BP Properties Ltd as having become registered proprietor of the "whole farm" in November 1982 and then determines the later adverse-possession dispute concerning the farmhouse and garden. It does not, however, determine whether the 1982 first-registration application had itself correctly included the farmhouse parcel in BP's documentary title, or whether the registration had mistakenly conflated two historically separate parcels.

That distinction is fundamental.

My family's parcel — the former farmhouse, garden and curtilage, which I refer to as the House Plot — was historically distinct from the adjoining eastern agricultural land. The documentary history I have obtained indicates that these areas were not simply one undifferentiated proprietary parcel.

The 1916 agricultural tenancy is one important document because it embraced both areas. But that is not the end of the conveyancing history. The earlier 1877 Daniel Thomas & Son instrument, and the arrangement subsequently acted upon when the quarrying ceased in 1928, point to a separate proprietary interest in the House Plot. 

I have the 1938 conveyance from the Marquis of Bute to Western Ground Rents, and the revised 1939 version of the 1916 tenancy, and it did not convey or demise the House Plot at all: the actual 1938 conveyance, the 1939 tenancy and their plans need to be examined by you lot too, not just me. Indeed, the 1987 judgment itself records that the alleged yearly tenancy commencing in 1949 has not been produced in the proceedings. Its geographical extent therefore remains unproved. Not withstanding it may pertain to the parcel to the east we leased and defaulted on, not our freehold parcel. Furthermore my nan expressly rejected the 1949 tenancy and attempt to make her occupancy of our parcel permissive in such a way, but expressly rejecting it while asserting her ownership claim of her parcel. 

It's adolescent of everyone to keep having a meltdown and failing to compute the simplicity of the fact Mary Williams asserted she owned her parcel. And WGR saught possession of theirs, east of it. Western Ground Rents, already described in UK Parliament as praying on elderly and being abhorrent and scrupilous, clearly tried to make Mary's occupany appear permissive in 1949 and the 1955  proceedings.

The 1987 judgment records that and the 1962 proceeding, after the agricultural tenancy was terminated, as Western Ground Rents obtaining a 1955 possession order for the "whole of the farm". Crucially, however, when that order was enforced on 4 July 1955, possession was taken of all parts except the farmhouse and garden. The judgment gives the immediate reason as Mrs Mary Buckler's condition and her strong resistance to leaving the farmhouse. Ambiguity which is later misinterprited and clearly an early attempt at making her occupancy of her parcel appear permissive. 

WGR subsequently brought a fresh action in 1962 specifically against Mr and Mrs  Buckler for possession of the farmhouse and garden and mesne profits, resulting in the possession and mesne-profits order of 11 December 1962. The judgment records that this order was not enforced before 1974.

That sequence matters.

If the two areas had genuinely always constituted one undifferentiated proprietary estate subject to the same right of possession, it is difficult to understand why possession of the agricultural land was recovered in 1955 while the farmhouse and garden were left occupied and a separate possession action had to be brought in 1962.

I therefore ask that this fact not be retrospectively converted into an assumption that the 1955 "whole farm" wording necessarily comprised the House Plot in the same legal sense as the agricultural land.

The statutory effect attributed by the Court of Appeal to the 1955/1962 proceedings cannot itself establish title to a different, historically separate parcel which was never actually comprised in those proceedings.

The possession orders were orders for possession and associated relief. They were not conveyances. They did not retrospectively create a documentary chain of title where none existed, nor did they by themselves determine the geographical extent of an underlying freehold documentary title.

That is especially important in light of the sequence of events recorded in the 1987 judgment. WGR's own successive proceedings and selective enforcement distinguished the agricultural land from the farmhouse and garden in practical terms, whatever the later interpretation of the expression "whole farm".

There is a further point which I believe HM Land Registry has not addressed.

In 1949, according to the history now being assembled, Mrs Mary Williams was offered a tenancy of the farmhouse and garden which she rejected because she asserted ownership. The 1987 judgment itself confirms that she was offered a tenancy of the farmhouse and garden by Western Ground Rents and refused it. It also records that she had come to believe she had a title through her grandfather and that documents existed which supported that claim.

Thus there was plainly a known dispute over the House Plot long before first registration.

The 1974 proceedings and letters must also be put in their proper place. The Court of Appeal held that the 1974 letters operated as a licence, notwithstanding that Mrs Buckler had never expressly accepted them, and held that her possession thereafter was no longer adverse. 

I am not asking HM Land Registry to disregard that decision.
