Made out to a non existent Mrs Buckler. And quashed the case within minutes of Mary being notified of them, with no ample opportunity to respond. Albeit she actually did in writing. And asserted her ownership and challenged BP in a public newspaper. Not withstanding BP couldn't give something they don't own i.e. permissive occupancy. 

This permissive occupancy followed by a conversion is a racket. Look at the pattern;

1955 permissive occupancy ploy > 1969 conveyance (WGR to BP Pension Trust Ltd)

1974 permissive occupancy ploy > 1975 conveyance (BP Pension Trust to BP Properties Ltd)

Nor am I asking the Land Registry to even acknowledge the fact court clerked notified the press who all decended on the scene, covered the story (that Mary asserted ownership, family occupancy since 1667, lawyer confirms her ownership claim was valid etc). 

I am asking a different question: what land did BP actually have title to in 1974, and what land was actually capable of being registered in BP's name in 1982?

If the House Plot had never formed part of WGR's documentary estate (not in the 1938 conveyance from Bute, as it went to Daniel Thomas & Son in 1876 then to my great grandad John Williams in 1928), then the 1974 letters and the 1962 possession order cannot simply be assumed to cure that problem. The 1987 judgment did not adjudicate that separate issue of first-registration procedure and documentary extent.

BP never had ownership. Ours ownership claim was never legally exstiguished. BP never even saught ownership, only possession. And with no title chain, only their own issuance of permissive occupancy, based on interest they'd purchased in a possession order, which itself was also based on issuance of permissive occupancy. And with little to no meeting of the minds, but instead stealth/ secrecy. And the registration itself in 1983 was secret and undisclosed to Mary Williams and us living heirs and successors. 

The Land Registry issue

The applicable statutory framework in 1982/83 was the Land Registration Act 1925 and the Land Registration Rules 1925.

The Rules expressly contained provisions dealing with first registration, including rule 20, requiring the applicant to deliver the original deeds and documents relating to the title which were in its possession or control. The operation of that rule in the first-registration context is confirmed in Walker v Burton, where the High Court described the requirement in those terms.

The Rules also contained a specific provision headed "Examination of title by Registrar" and provisions concerning searches and enquiries by the Registrar.

This means that the question cannot simply be reduced to "Land Registry registers what it is given".

The relevant question is whether, in this case:

  1. the applicant supplied the material title documents in its possession or control;

  2. the documents supplied actually demonstrated that the House Plot formed part of the estate being registered;

  3. the Registrar examined the documentary chain sufficiently to identify any inconsistency between the deeds and the land claimed for registration;

  4. any discrepancy between the deeds, plans, possession orders and the proposed registration plan generated a requisition or further enquiry;

  5. the registration was completed as an absolute title despite a material uncertainty as to the extent of the documentary title; and

  6. the Registrar's own records contain any warning, requisition, note, correspondence or other indication that the separate House Plot issue was considered.

There is a particularly important point concerning registration in error.

The Law Commission's review of the 1925 system records that the Land Registration Rules 1925 contained a specific power in rule 14 dealing with "registration in error", including registration of too large a part of a title, and explained that the registrar had an express power to rectify registration arising from mistake.

That is significant because HM Land Registry is currently saying, in effect, that there was no mistake. That conclusion should not be treated as established unless HM Land Registry has actually examined the surviving 1982/83 registration file and established what documentary evidence justified the extent registered.

HM Land Registry's present published guidance also expressly recognises that including too much land in a registered title can constitute a mistake in the register, and gives as an example a title being mapped to include land for which the registered proprietor has no documentary title. It also recognises that failure by a solicitor to lodge documents in their possession can amount to lack of proper care. I appreciate that this is modern guidance and I do not suggest that it can simply be imposed retrospectively as the law of 1983. It is nevertheless directly relevant to the distinction HM Land Registry now draws between a genuine registration mistake and a mere disagreement about the title boundary.

Likewise, HM Land Registry's current guidance states that a title plan cannot describe the land more accurately than the pre-registration deeds allow, and that the pre-registration deeds are crucial to resolving questions about the extent of a registered title. Again, I cite this as an expression of the documentary basis of registration, not as a claim that a 2025/26 practice guide was itself the governing rule in 1983.

Those entries require the original plans to be compared with the House Plot.

I am particularly concerned that two separate conveyancing areas were subsequently presented as part of a single "whole farm" registered estate. If the House Plot was not actually comprised in the conveyances relied upon, the relevant question is not whether the modern red edging can be made to fit an Ordnance Survey map. The question is what deed, order or other legally sufficient evidence put that specific land into BP's registrable estate in the first place.

An Ordnance Survey description cannot by itself create a conveyance. Much like BPs 1971 alteration of the descriptor of our parcel, shifting "ty mawr" from theirs to ours and appending "farm" to the end of it. 

Nor can a later registration description retrospectively supply a missing link in the pre-registration conveyancing chain.

I'll repeat this as its important; 

Nor can a later registration description retrospectively supply a missing link in the pre-registration conveyancing chain.

The 1982/83 registration file

HM Land Registry's letter of 30 July 2026, reference N610CGV, has already confirmed that surviving first-registration material relating to the relevant titles exists and is open to inspection.

I therefore ask you to write again to HM Land Registry, not asking it to decide the family title, but asking it to answer the following precise administrative questions:

1. What exact first-registration applications were made for WA231076 and WA240304, and what deeds, abstracts, declarations, plans, court orders and other documents accompanied each application?

3. What document was relied upon to establish that the House Plot formed part of BP Properties Limited's documentary estate? How was Land Registry not able to see only a plaintiff on the court paperwork preceeding 1982, and no defendant?

5. Were the Registrar's records aware of the 1974 proceedings and Mrs Williams  asserted ownership claim when the first-registration applications were processed? 

The only way they could have not been is if they willfully ignorantly and selective vision didn't see there was another party to the court proceedings, not just a claimant but also a defendant. They/ BP will have had to have fished out a 1935 marriage certificate to find anything to match the name Mrs Buckler, on the licence letters. A deperate measure to avoid any of this clandestine registration reaching the families knowledge, which we would have been very quick to correct all this. And low and behold she did conveniently die in the two weeks she will have had to challenge this in 1983. I guess someone murdered her, just to be absolutely sure all this went ahead without any issues.

9. Does HM Land Registry's surviving file contain any memorandum, examiner's note, requisition, map correspondence or other record explaining how the apparently separate areas were reconciled into the registered extent?

Dear Information Rights Unit,

To keep everything for the Welsh Government in one place, this email covers four things: (A) a request for an internal review of ATISN 26-0010; (B) ATISN 27589 (Cadw; your ref qA2496208); (C) four new requests for information; and (D) a request that records be preserved. I would be grateful if you could pass each part to the right team.

A. ATISN 26-0010 – request for internal review

Thank you, and please pass my thanks to Emma Harvey-Woodason, for the response of 19 October 2026. I ask for an internal review on four points. Each asks only for recorded information, or for confirmation that none is held.

1. Item 2 of my request asked for any recorded information on whether files in those series were destroyed, transferred or retained, and if destroyed "the date and authority". The response says "any routine records would have been destroyed in line with the corporate retention schedule applied at the time", and that it is "equally possible" that disposition "would have been carried out by a predecessor body". Please confirm whether the Welsh Government holds any record of an actual destruction, transfer or retention decision for files in those series relating to the farm, Western Ground Rents Ltd or BP Properties Ltd. If none is held, please confirm that the quoted sentences describe the likely position and not a recorded event.

2. If a specific entry in a retention schedule was relied on for the sentence quoted at point 1, please provide that entry (title, version, date). If no particular entry was identified, please say so. I have noted that the current schedules are published on GOV.WALES, so I am not asking you to explain them.

3. The response says that "Before 1997, the Welsh Office or other agencies … would have had their own retention schedules." Does the Welsh Government hold the Welsh Office schedules for the file series in item 1 of my request? If so, please provide them. If not, please say so and, if known, where they are held.

4. The response says: "Searches were carried out to find files mentioning the farm name and the companies listed in your request." Please provide the record of those searches: the systems, indexes and file series searched, the search terms, the date range, and whether the index of physical registered files was included. (The internal review of ATISN 27021, dated 2 July 2026, describes searches of physical registered files, including A--CL172-06-017/1 Community of Llandough, and a wider search of files from around the 1980s–1990s.)

For the avoidance of doubt, the 1988 Cadw listing file is not part of this review; it is covered by ATISN 26-0009 (response due 6 November 2026).

B. ATISN 27589 (Cadw; your ref qA2496208)

I note the letter of 19 October 2026 refusing ATISN 27589 under section 14(2). Three points, so that I can decide whether to ask for an internal review:

1. Section 14(2) applies only to a request that is substantially similar to an earlier one. Please tell me which points of ATISN 27589 the Welsh Government considers ATISN 27021 already covered. Point 3 of ATISN 27589 asked for "Any transfer, destruction or disposal of those files, with the schedule used and the date." ATISN 27021 did not ask for that.

2. The letter says that no new information "has been generated or become available". Please confirm whether it is saying that no information is held on any point of ATISN 27589 beyond what was released under ATISN 27021, or only that it declines to search again.

3. The letter sets out the right to complain to the Information Commissioner but not the internal review procedure, although it refers to the internal review of ATISN 27021. Please confirm how and by when I may ask for an internal review of ATISN 27589. I will not treat the time for asking as running until you have confirmed this.

The question in point 3 of ATISN 27589 is also being dealt with under ATISN 26-0009, so I am not making any new request about it here.

C. New requests under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and the Environmental Information Regulations 2004

These are new requests and not part of the review above. They concern Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Vale of Glamorgan.

1. Registered files. The internal review of ATISN 27021 identified registered files (including A--CL172-06-017/1 Community of Llandough, CL172-10-001/1, A--CL172-10-002/1, A--CL172-10-001/1, and six files of potential interest). I am not asking for the contents of the files. For each file, please provide the register entry or index record showing its title, opening and closing dates, and current status (retained, transferred, destroyed or not traced) and, where the entry says a file was destroyed or transferred, the date and the record of the destruction or transfer.

2. Property and deeds records. The response to ATISN 26-0010 says that records of Welsh Government property, deeds and leasing are retained until the property is sold or the lease ends. Please confirm whether the Welsh Government or the Welsh Office has ever owned, leased, acquired or disposed of any interest in land at Great House Farm, Leckwith Road or village green VG41, Llandough, between 1950 and 1997, and provide any deed, lease or property file record of it. If none is held, please say so.

3. Wartime farm records, 1936–1955. Please provide any recorded information held by the Welsh Government, including records inherited from the Welsh Office, about the farm in 1936–1955:
(a) any record of the Glamorgan War Agricultural Executive Committee, or its post-war successor, about the farm, including any possession, requisition or cultivation direction;
(b) any claim or payment under the Compensation (Defence) Act 1939;
(c) any record naming the occupier or owner of the farm in that period.
I understand the 1941–43 National Farm Survey is held at The National Archives (MAF 32), so I am not asking for it. If any other record has been transferred to The National Archives, please give the reference rather than treating that part as not held.

4. Compulsory purchase and stopping-up orders, 1950–1995. Please confirm whether the Secretary of State for Wales or the Welsh Office made or confirmed any compulsory purchase order, stopping-up order or diversion order affecting the land at Great House Farm between 1950 and 1995, and provide a copy of any such order and of the decision confirming it. ATISN 26-0010 searched under the farm name and two company names. Orders of this kind are usually titled by road or place, so please also search under "Leckwith Road, Llandough", "Llandough-juxta-Penarth" and "Church View Close". If such records have been transferred to The National Archives, please give the reference.

If no information is held for any part, please say so. If anything is withheld, please give the exemption or exception relied on.

D. Preservation of records

As I asked on 28 September and 1 October 2026, please make sure that the following are not destroyed or weeded while ATISN 26-0009, the review in part A, the requests in part C and any complaint to the Information Commissioner remain open:

1. the index of physical registered files, and the registered files themselves, referred to in the internal review of ATISN 27021 (including A--CL172-06-017/1, CL172-10-001/1, A--CL172-10-002/1, A--CL172-10-001/1 and the six files of potential interest identified in that review);
2. any 1988 listing file for Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, or any part or remnant of it;
3. the originals of the two inspection photographs dated 29 July 1988 released under ATISN 27021, with any negatives, digital files, envelopes, captions or other information recorded with them;
4. any disposal or destruction logs, certificates or schedules of destruction covering Welsh Office or Cadw records for 1970–1997;
5. the retention schedules in force for those records in 1970–1997;
6. any transfer lists to The National Archives or a Place of Deposit for those records, including any selection records made under OSP 7.

Please confirm in writing that a hold is in place for these records.

Thank you for your help.

Yours sincerely,

Dear Calli,

Further to my email of 8 September 2026 concerning Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, I attach a formal schedule of the records I am seeking, so that the request is easier for Heneb to work through and to allocate internally. I have also completed your online enquiry form, so the request is in your preferred channel.

I appreciate a response would not fall due until 6 October, so this is not a chaser. It is to put the detail in one place and to clarify the basis of the request.

On your note of 22 May. You are right that Heneb, as a limited company, is not a public authority under the Freedom of Information Act 2000, and I do not pursue that. Two separate points remain, and I would welcome Heneb's position on each.

First, the Environmental Information Regulations 2004 apply on a different test — regulation 2(2) reaches bodies carrying out functions of public administration relating to the environment, or under the control of a public authority. If Heneb considers it falls outside that, please say so expressly with brief reasons, so that I can direct the request elsewhere.

Second, and independently, the Historic Environment Record is a statutory record: sections 194 and 195 of the Historic Environment (Wales) Act 2023 require the Welsh Ministers to maintain an HER for every local authority area and to make it available for public inspection, and Heneb keeps the south-east Wales record on their behalf. I therefore ask in the alternative that this be treated as a request for access under that regime and under Heneb's own policy.

Two things that will make this easier. If any item is too broad, please tell me which and I will narrow it rather than have the whole request refused. And if Heneb can supply, as a first step, simply a schedule or index of the records it holds for this site — without copying them — that would let me target the rest precisely and save your staff considerable time. I am content to inspect material by appointment at Baglan or at the HER, and any reasonable copying or staff-time charge can be notified to me in advance for approval.

Two small administrative points. Please confirm which legal entity now holds the records and functions formerly of Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust Ltd, and who within Heneb handles access requests of this kind.

Finally, since my correspondence in May was framed more formally: my purpose is documentary. I am reconstructing the record of a farm my family occupied for generations, and I would far rather do that with Heneb's help than around it.

I should say plainly that I have read GGAT's December 1993 notification to the Vale of Glamorgan that Condition 18 had not been complied with, and the recommendation that a Breach of Condition Notice be issued. Whatever else is in dispute about this site, that was the Trust doing its job properly, and I am grateful for it.

Thank you in advance for your time in this matter,

Regards,

Dear Mr Egan, Thank you for your email confirming that the Council meeting on 22 October 2026 will now be held remotely only. I object to the removal of the opportunity for residents to attend in person and ask that the decision be reconsidered before the meeting. I recognise that the Local Government and Elections (Wales) Act 2021 provides for remote meetings. Subject: Preservation notice — Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough — do not destroy records — Matter of public interest


FORMAL PRESERVATION NOTICE
Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth
Titles: WA231076, WA240304, WA513690 and WA735527
Planning references: 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES

URL: greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com 

To each recipient separately, in your own capacity as a current or potential holder, custodian or controller of relevant records:

This notice is addressed to each recipient individually. It is not a joint request, and it does not ask any recipient to speak for, investigate on behalf of, or answer in place of any other person or organisation. Each recipient is asked to respond only in respect of records within that recipient's own possession, custody or control, including records inherited from a predecessor organisation or retained on its behalf.

1. Nature and purpose of this notice

This is a formal preservation notice concerning documentary material relating to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, adjoining St Dochdwy's, and the subsequent development of the site, including the area now associated with Church View Close.

It is not a claim form, is not service of proceedings, and is not intended to constitute or replace any FOI request, internal review, complaint, subject-access request or other statutory process already made to any recipient.

The purpose of this notice is to require the preservation of potentially relevant material while the documentary history, title chain, registration history, planning history, possession proceedings, demolition and subsequent development are being reconstructed.

A separate first-stage preservation notice has been issued or is being issued to Cadw / Welsh Government FOI, HM Land Registry Wales Office and DPO, Heneb / GGAT HER, RCAHMW, Vale of Glamorgan FOI Unit and DPO, Glamorgan Archives, South Wales Police FOI, The National Archives, the Wales Office FOI team, and the National Library of Wales. Persimmon Homes (Wales) Ltd has received a separate preservation letter.

You are receiving this notice separately because the published documentary record places you, or a predecessor whose records may remain in your custody or control, within the documentary, legal, professional, administrative or development chain concerning this land.

2. Land and documentary scope

Please preserve, and do not destroy, alter, overwrite, discard, transfer out of custody without a recorded handover, or otherwise dispose of, any record within your possession, custody or control relating to the land or matters identified below.

The scope includes, without limitation, originals, copies, working papers, drafts, annotations, plans, photographs, negatives, films, tapes, maps, registers, indexes, correspondence, emails and attachments, electronic files, archived mailboxes, databases, metadata, internal notes, meeting records, instructions, client or matter files, survey material and other associated records.

The material requested includes:

1. Historical ownership, occupation and conveyancing

The 1877 split; the 1916 and 1939 tenancies; the 1938 Bute to Western Ground Rents conveyance; the 1969 Western Ground Rents to BP Pension Trust conveyance; and any plans, schedules, abstracts, searches, correspondence or other documents relied upon in relation to those transactions.

2. Possession proceedings and subsequent litigation

The 1955 High Court and 1962 Cardiff County Court possession orders; the 1974 proceedings; BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2; House of Lords leave papers, including YHL/PO/JO/10/11/2536; and Buckler v United Kingdom (1989), including associated correspondence, instructions, evidence, plans and working papers.

3. Land registration

The first registration of WA231076, including the application dated 30 November 1982; the first registration of WA240304, including the application dated 23 February 1983; subsequent amalgamation, transfer or closure; and every plan, conveyance, abstract, search, application, correspondence trail or professional file relied upon in connection with those registrations or changes.

4. 1988 possession and demolition

The taking of possession on or about 29 November 1988 and the demolition commenced on or about 6 December 1988, including any planning, listed-building, heritage, police, enforcement, media, contractor, survey, photographic or inter-agency liaison material.

5. Planning and subsequent development, 1989–1996

Planning application 89/01396/OUT; reserved matters application 92/00671/RES; conditions 16–18; GGAT / Cotswold Archaeology material; records concerning any section 52, section 106, planning obligation, local land charge or equivalent instrument; and the transfer from BP to Ideal Homes dated 3 December 1993, together with all associated plans, correspondence, approvals, agreements, searches and completion material.

6. Family records

Records concerning Mary Doreen Williams (died 1983) and William Buckler, insofar as those records relate to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, the land described above, its occupation, ownership, possession, disposal, registration, development or demolition.

3. Predecessor and inherited files

Where you hold, or may hold, a file originating with a predecessor, successor, merged practice, affiliated practice, client or other entity, that material is also within scope.

This includes, without limitation, records originating from:

Loosemores of Cardiff; Robbins Olivey & Blake Lapthorn / Blake Morgan; Linklaters & Paines; Debenham Tewson / DTZ / Cushman & Wakefield; Wyn Thomas + Partners; Ideal Homes Wales; BP Properties; BP Pension Trust; Cotswold Archaeological Trust; Cardiff Bay Development Corporation; and South Glamorgan County Council.

The reference to a predecessor file does not assert that you necessarily hold such a file. It identifies material for which a reasonable custody or succession inquiry should be made where applicable.

4. Preservation steps

Please take reasonable steps to prevent the routine destruction, deletion, alteration or overwriting of potentially relevant material, including material held in archived mailboxes, legacy systems, off-site storage, document-management systems, backup repositories and other electronic or physical stores.

Where relevant material has been transferred to another repository, archive, successor organisation or third party, please preserve the information necessary to identify the transfer and its current location, including any accession, file, box, reference or custody details.

Nothing in this notice requires the creation of records that do not exist. The request concerns the preservation of records already held or controlled by you.

5. Purpose and legal position

This notice is not a finding against any recipient, and I am not asking any recipient to determine title or adjudicate the underlying dispute.

The 1987 Court of Appeal judgment is relied upon here only for matters actually determined by that judgment, including the issues concerning possession, limitation and the October 1974 letters. This preservation notice does not treat that judgment as having determined the complete documentary root of title to the farmhouse parcel.

The underlying documentary history, including the relationship between the farmhouse parcel and the agricultural land subsequently dealt with through Western Ground Rents and BP, remains a matter requiring reconstruction from the primary records.

Accordingly, preservation is requested precisely so that the documentary record can be established from the records themselves rather than through assumptions based on later registration, later occupation, later planning treatment or secondary descriptions.

6. Acknowledgement and identification of records

Please acknowledge receipt of this notice and, in your own capacity, confirm:

(a) the officer, partner, records manager or other person responsible for implementing the preservation hold;

(b) what records within your possession, custody or control you have identified as falling within the scope above; and

(c) where you identify no records within scope, what relevant systems, files, repositories or predecessor records you searched in reaching that conclusion.

A substantive assessment of title is not requested from you. The immediate requirement is preservation and identification of the documentary material you hold.

The public documentary index and developing evidence record is available at:

https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/

Please monitor that site for subsequent identification of documents, references and specific schedules relevant to your organisation's records.

Where a reliable public email address is unavailable, a postal preservation notice will also be sent. For example, a postal notice will follow to Loosemores, Alliance House, 18–19 High Street, Cardiff [postcode redacted].

Nothing in this notice constitutes an abandonment, waiver or limitation of any claim, position or remedy concerning title, registration, concealment, limitation, reopening, rectification or alteration of the register, or any associated matter.

Regards,

Requester

Dear Owen and Nia,

Thank you, Owen, for speaking with me. I have now examined the catalogue
information for another item held by the National Library of Wales, and it
helps clarify why I need to distinguish the different recordings,
broadcasts and later publications.

I want to establish what happened to the reporting, what actually aired,
what survives, and when the material was disclosed or made publicly
accessible. I am raising concerns and asking questions, not asserting that
deliberate censorship or a special non-disclosure agreement has been proved.

*The omissions and editorial questions*

My principal concern is that the coverage I have seen does not convey the
full human circumstances of the events. In particular, three infant
children and the fact that my mother was pregnant at the time appear to
have been omitted.

I am also concerned about the apparently abrupt edit following the
reference to the property as prime development land overlooking Cardiff
Bay. I would like to establish whether that cut appeared in the original
broadcast or was introduced when a later viewing copy was edited.

There is a further personal dimension involving Nicola Heywood-Thomas, the
presenter identified in the material. For a period, she was like a second
mother to me. That connection is important to my understanding of the
story, although I recognise that the existence of a personal relationship
does not, in itself, establish what the broadcaster knew or was required to
include. I would like to know whether footage involving her was broadcast,
whether other versions survive, and whether any relevant editorial or
confidentiality record exists.

*The chronology I need to reconcile*

The following are separate events and records, and I would be grateful for
your help establishing their precise relationship.

   -

   *30 November 1988 — eviction and injunction coverage.* The National
   Library of Wales Watch and Listen catalogue has an item entitled *Eviction
   News Material, 30 November 1988*:
   https://gwylio-gwrando.llyfrgell.cymru/detail/507738. Its catalogue
   dates recording and broadcast to 30 November. It describes a one-minute HTV
   Wales Betacam item involving Miles Fletcher, bailiffs removing furniture,
   removal vans and [member of the public] leaving the farm. The abstract refers to a
   High Court injunction preventing demolition.

   Crucially, the cataloguer says “Not viewed”. The tape contains unrelated
   clips, the position of this particular clip is unknown, and the description
   may have been taken from the broadcaster’s log. The record does not supply
   a catalogue-creation date or online-publication date.
   -

   *5 December 1988 — separate demolition report.* I am investigating a
   distinct *Wales at Six* demolition headline/report and the associated
   off-transmission recording. I do not want the 30 November eviction and
   injunction item mistaken for the 5 December demolition coverage. I would
   like to establish whether the latter report aired, whether the surviving
   material represents the complete broadcast, and whether scripts, running
   orders, transmission logs or rushes survive.
   -

   *6 December 1988 — demolition.* This is the recorded date of the
   farmhouse demolition in the heritage record. The event date should be kept
   separate from filming, broadcast and archival dates.
   -

   *25 July 2025 — National Library of Wales YouTube publication.* The
   viewing copy I have identified as 4GXmR7mAas0 is associated with this
   publication date. The relevant link is https://youtu.be/4GXmR7mAas0. I
   understand the online publication was by the National Library of Wales, not
   an ITV upload. I would like the uploader and publication metadata retained
   and checked, and the exact relationship between this copy and the catalogue
   item above established.
   -

   *Archive donation and digitisation.* The National Library of Wales holds
   ITV Wales/HTV material following the archive donation announced in 2012. I
   would like to know whether the specific recordings under discussion were
   included in that transfer, and whether their individual accession,
   digitisation and catalogue histories are available.
   -

   *My disclosure requests and subsequent contacts.* I would like the
   requests, responses, referrals and any internal handling records reconciled
   against these individual items. A later public upload does not, by itself,
   answer whether the footage was previously disclosed to me or when the
   Library’s catalogue entry became accessible online.

I also note that Owen’s reported reference to a December 2025 YouTube
publication does not match the 25 July 2025 date associated with the
viewing copy identified above. These dates should not be assigned to the
same item until we establish precisely which video was meant.

*What I would appreciate from ITV Wales*

Please help establish:

   1. The transmission date, programme, duration and running order for the
   1988 eviction/injunction report and the separate 5 December demolition
   report.
   2. Whether ITV holds the complete broadcasts, off-transmission masters,
   scripts, rushes, outtakes, edit histories or other versions.
   3. Whether the abrupt cut around the property’s development value was
   present in the original broadcast or belongs to a later edit.
   4. Whether relevant footage involving Nicola Heywood-Thomas aired, and
   whether any alternative version survives.
   5. Whether any relevant editorial instruction, contractual restriction
   or case-specific non-disclosure agreement exists. I am asking whether such
   a record exists, not asserting that one does.
   6. What ITV records show about receiving, routing and handling my
   disclosure requests.
   7. Whether ITV can identify the specific items transferred to the
   National Library of Wales and provide any available provenance or accession
   information.

I would also welcome guidance on the best way to coordinate these enquiries
with Beryl Evans and the National Library of Wales Enquiries team,
particularly concerning the creation and first online publication of
catalogue record 507738 and the search for separate 5 December material.

The Library’s stated restrictions on viewing original media and reusing
footage may be entirely routine. They do not, by themselves, establish
concealment or unusual treatment. Equally, the existence of a public
catalogue entry does not settle the questions about broadcast completeness,
the history of my disclosure requests or the publication dates of
individual items.

I am seeking a reliable chronology and an accurate account of the surviving
evidence. If any part of my understanding is mistaken, I would welcome a
clear correction supported by the relevant record. If a record cannot be
found or no longer survives, please distinguish that from a question that
has not yet been searched.

Thank you for your help. Please let me know who will coordinate the
enquiries and which records ITV can realistically investigate.

Kind regards,

Requester

2. The 1983 record on your own schedule

- 23 February 1983: form 1C application from Linklaters & Paines (WA240304 item 11), and a register edition of the same date (item 10).
- 26 March 1983: Mary Williams, the occupier of the farmhouse, died.
- 8 April 1983: form D23 ("inside exam") and a Linklaters & Paines letter (WA240304 item 7).
- 12 April 1983: customer correspondence (item 4), plus undated letters (item 5).

- 13 January 1984: form A3 application (item 15) and a new register edition (item 23).
- 22 May 1984: BP's writ for possession. This is chronology only, not evidence of what the Registry knew in 1983.
- 2 February 1987: application to amalgamate (WA231076 item 14). Your schedule says the WA240304 copy of the form has "no annotation on it".

3. Points arising

3.1 Root of title and class of title. Raised before: my email of 16 September (points 10 and 13) and my ICR referral. NEW detail: your stage one letter says a full documentary title commencing with a good root at least 15 years old should normally establish title. It then concluded a good root was shown and that BP Pension Trust acquired the land in 1969. That conclusion rests on the recital in the 1975 conveyance, which refers to a conveyance of 31 December 1969. The 1969 deed itself is not on your schedule. The recited root was about 13 years 2 months old on 23 February 1983. The letter also quotes the 1975 recital as giving the year as "One thousand One hundred and sixty nine". Please confirm the original reads 1969. Please say which documents the Registry relied on as the root, whether any exception or alternative procedure was used (and under which provision of the 1925 Act), why absolute title was accepted, and the class of title first entered for WA240304.

3.2 The 1971 abstract. Raised before: 30 July, 12 August and 16 September (points 1 and 8). Your letter says a 1971 abstract was lodged with the WA231076 application and that the Registry "had sight of" one for WA240304. Neither schedule lists it. NEW: a 1971 abstract cannot evidence a conveyance of 1975. What evidenced that conveyance?

3.3 Extent and plans. Raised before in part: 18 September. NEW: WA240304 item 1 is a plan to the conveyance of 23 May 1975, but item 13 is a plan "to conveyance dated 23 February 1975". Please reconcile those dates and say which plan governed the registration. The WA231076 register records that the 1975 conveyance plan is "filed under WA240304", which is now a closed title. Please supply the original title plan (item 9) and both plans. Please also identify the land conveyed in 1975 and the vendors' "Retained Land", the capacity in which each vendor conveyed, and how the extents of the two titles related immediately before amalgamation, including any overlap. The register also records that a new filed plan was substituted on 5 January 1995. Please supply the plan it replaced and confirm the extent did not change.

3.4 The occupier and what the Registry knew. Raised before in part: 16 September (points 4 and 12), 27 September, and ICR/090/26. Mary Williams was in actual occupation of the farmhouse in February and March 1983. The history includes the 1955 order against Frederick Buckler alone, the 1962 order against Frederick and Mary for the farmhouse and garden (not enforced), and the 1974 county court action in which Mary pleaded ownership, which was part-heard and never concluded. NEW: stage two says the Registry "were unaware of any dispute that was possibly ongoing". Yet WA240304 holds an inside examination (D23) and letters of 8 and 12 April 1983, and WA231076 holds letters between the applicant's solicitors and the Registry of 12 May 1983. Please say what enquiry was made of the occupier (Land Registration Act 1925 s.70(1)(g)), what inspection was done, and what those letters said about occupation, possession proceedings or the 1974 action. Please supply the D23 examination record.

3.5 The solicitors' certificate. Raised before: 30 July and 16 September (points 2 and 9). Stage one relied on certificate wording from form FR1. The 1983 application was on form 1C. Please supply form 1C as lodged and say what it certified about any question or doubt affecting title.

3.6 Notice and caution. Raised before: my email of 27 September (the family's case) and ICR/090/26. NEW: stage two says my family could have applied for a caution. That requires knowing of the application. Please produce every notice and service record for WA240304, as sent, showing the title it concerned, the addressee's name, the address, the date and any proof of delivery. A notice addressed to Mary Williams and issued or received after 26 March 1983 went to a person who had died. If it went to "Mrs Williams" at the property, I ask whether that was the right name and the right household. I am not asserting that this happened. I am asking for the record.

3.7 The 1987 judgment and the amalgamation. Raised before: 16 September (point 14) and ICR/090/26. Stage one said it is not for the Registrar to look behind decisions of the Court. The Court of Appeal considered adverse possession, the 1962 order and the 1974 letters. As I read it, it did not review the Registry's examination of title, the documents supplied or the notices. Please say precisely what HMLR says that judgment established and which parts of its 1983 process it says the judgment answers. NEW: please provide the application, decision and completion dates of the amalgamation, the instrument and plans relied on, the power used, and whether the registered extent changed or only the structure of the register. HMLR has also given the closure of WA240304 as 1987 (the amalgamation) and as 2005 (your email of 21 September 2026, enquiry 260919-6726246). Please state the actual date and the entry that records it.

3.8 What the complaint decisions examined. Raised before: ICR/090/26. The itemised schedule reached me on 30 July 2026, after both decisions. NEW: stage two says the reviewer examined "the evidence lodged in support of the application". Please confirm which original first-registration documents each decision-maker examined, whether the absence of the 1969 conveyance was identified, and provide the recorded basis for the conclusions reached.

3.9 The 1994 corrections. NEW to the Registry (raised only with the ICR). WA231076 items 12 and 22 are applications "to correct the title", dated 20 January 1994 and 13 October 1994. Stage one and stage two found no evidence of a mistake. Please say what was corrected, on whose application, under what authority, on what evidence, and whether the registered extent changed, including land derived from WA240304.

4. Schedule 4 (mistake and rectification) and Schedule 8 (indemnity). NEW

A. Mistake. I understand Schedule 4 now governs alteration of the register as it stands, including entries made in 1983 under the 1925 Act. The Registrar may alter the register to correct a mistake (paragraph 5(a)). Practice Guide 39 gives "including too much land in a registered title" as an example. I say there is a possible mistake in the 1983 entry in two respects: absolute title entered on a root that is not on the file (3.1 and 3.2), and an extent fixed by plans that do not reconcile (3.3). Please state whether HMLR accepts either as a mistake.

B. Possession and proper care. Practice Guide 39 (sections 1.3 and 1.4) says a registered proprietor in possession is protected unless it caused or contributed to the mistake by fraud or lack of proper care, or unless it would be unjust not to correct. Possession means physical possession. Please say who is in physical possession of the land affected. Practice Guide 39 (appendix 12.3.1) gives as an example a solicitor on a first registration who fails to lodge all the documents in their possession. Please say whether the applicant's solicitors lodged every document in their possession in 1983, including the 1969 conveyance and the abstract, and whether HMLR considers that bears on this protection. I do not assert that anything was withheld.

C. Class of title and overriding interests. Practice Guide 39 (section 1.1) says an alteration can give effect to an estate, right or interest not affected by registration where land is registered with good leasehold, possessory or qualified title. If the root evidence supported no more than that, the class entered may itself be the mistake. Section 1.2 says an alteration reflecting an overriding interest is not rectification. Please say whether HMLR accepts that an occupier's rights in 1983 could be recorded without that being rectification, and how it would deal with them.

D. Indemnity and process. Please confirm Z084NQV is being treated as a formal application for alteration, or tell me what form and fee are required (Practice Guide 39 section 2.1; rule 13 of the Land Registration Rules 2003). Practice Guide 39 says anyone may apply, and the fee may be refunded where the Registry caused the error. Indemnity time runs for six years from when the claimant knew or should have known of the claim (Schedule 8 paragraph 8). The family first saw the file schedule on 30 July 2026. Please confirm HMLR will treat any claim as in time. Please also give your consent under Schedule 8 paragraph 3 to reasonable costs, including copy fees at £11 per document. Where indemnity is not available, please consider whether a payment for maladministration is appropriate (Practice Guide 39 section 11).

5. Anticipated responses

- "The amalgamation was administrative tidying." Points 3.3 and 3.7 ask whether it altered the registered extent. Points 3.1 and 3.2 go to the examination of title, not to the structure of the register.
- "The missing documents' contents are unknown, so absence of evidence is not evidence of absence." That is why I ask for the files to be read and the examination record produced.
- "The Registry may rely on the solicitors' certificate." Please produce the certificate actually given on form 1C (3.5).
- "The registrar may approve a title open to objection where the holding is unlikely to be disturbed (section 13 of the 1925 Act, and section 9(3) of the 2002 Act)." If HMLR relied on that discretion, please identify the defect considered, the contemporaneous evidence supporting the opinion that the holding would not be disturbed, and the recorded reasons for approving the title. Please also explain how the occupier's rights under section 70(1)(g) were examined before they were treated as undisclosed.

6. Requests

(a) Confirm these points are added to Z084NQV, and confirm receipt of this email.
(b) Answer each numbered point and A to D, or say the record is not held.
(c) Provide copies of the WA240304 register as first registered, form 1C as lodged, form D23, the letters of 8 and 12 April 1983 and 12 May 1983, the A3 application of 13 January 1984 and the register edition, the 1971 abstract, both plans, the original title plan, every notice and service record, the amalgamation application with its decision and completion dates, and the two 1994 correction applications. If copies cannot be emailed, please give the OC2 / HC1 wording and the address for each.
(d) Reply within 20 working days.

Please also keep every document on both first-registration files and every related internal record, in line with my preservation notices of 3 June and 28 September 2026.

To the Independent Complaints Reviewer: please confirm whether you will consider this additional material in ICR/090/26, or whether I should raise it separately.

Yours faithfully,

Requester

Vale of Glamorgan Council

8th October 2026


Dear both

Illegal firework usage in Llandough

I’m saddened to report that another firework related incident took place in Llandough last night.

This is impacting some of the most vulnerable members of our community, causing distress to the elderly, small children and animals.

It is apparent that those responsible for setting off fireworks are not residents and instead come into the community from outside.

A lack of action to date is sending a message to those responsible that their behaviour is acceptable and will be tolerated.

There have been several instances in which fireworks have been set off past 11.00pm at night, in direct contravention of the law. There may also be other laws and regulations that have been broken.

I would therefore be grateful if you would:

- Outline full details of all firework-related incidents in the Llandough ward reported to your respective authorities within the past 24 months;

- Confirm all actions that were taken following those incidents to address the problems reported;

- Outline all actions proposed by your authorities to prevent inappropriate firework usage in the Llandough ward in future;

- Confirm all measures available to your respective authorities to detain and apprehend the individuals responsible for inappropriate firework usage in the Community of Llandough as well as any restrictions that may be imposed to prohibit those individuals from entering the Community boundary; and

- Confirm details of any powers conferred on your respective authorities which enable you to introduce additional regulations or byelaws to impose stricter restrictions prohibiting firework usage within the Community of Llandough.

I have not copied this message to our PSCOs because they are not responsible for operational decisions, and as such it would be unfair to attribute blame to them for the failure to address this problem.

However, I reiterate my request for your respective authorities to meet with me at the earliest convenience to discuss this ongoing problem, with an invitation also extended to our PCSOs.

Thank you for your consideration of this matter, and I look forward to your prompt response.

Kind regards,

Cllr George Carroll
Elected member

Llandough ward
Vale of Glamorgan Council

Great House Farm, Llandough

Sirs/ Ma'ams,


I need to correct a date I have used in earlier correspondence about Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, titles WA231076 and WA240304.


I had treated 1983 as the year the two titles were merged. That was wrong. HM Land Registry’s own letter of 23 March 2026 (Lisa Griffiths, ref N610CGV) separates the two acts.
1982–83 was first registration of two live titles, not a merger.
30 November 1982: application to first-register WA231076. The Court of Appeal later treated BP Properties Ltd as registered proprietors of “the farm” from November 1982.
23 February 1983: application to first-register a second title, WA240304.
26 March 1983: Mary Williams died. On the family’s case, notice of those applications did not reach us until after her death, while the family was in mourning. She had no window in which to object. The family was not in a position to use any window that arrived after that.
Those two titles remained separate through first instance.
24 July 1986: Hollis J. Both titles were still live. The judgment language treats Great House Farm as one holding. It had not been one holding on the register. On the family’s case it had not been one holding since the 1877 split: Parcel A (house, buildings, garden/yard and about 10 acres, the Thomas/Williams line) and Parcel B (the eastern fields retained by Bute and later WGR/BP).
2 February 1987: application to amalgamate the two titles. WA240304 was then closed and registration continued under WA231076. That is the merge. It was made after the 1986 ruling and before the Court of Appeal gave judgment on 31 July 1987.
So 1983 is silent first registration of a second title while Mary was still in Parcel A, or had only just died. 1987 is the administrative merger, carried out while the appeal was still open.
This was not a dispute about a single land parcel that BP already owned. Mary was on Parcel A, which the family says she owned, with occupation on that house parcel running in the family from at least 1667. BP, and WGR before it from 1949, were the neighbouring interest on Parcel B. From 1949 onwards the family’s case is that those neighbours ran a decades-long series of tenancy offers, “whole farm” wording, possession orders and the 1974 letters to make her occupation of her own parcel look permissive, and to make both parcels look like one estate they had acquired. They never produced a conveyance of Parcel A. What they had was an unfounded claim that her occupancy was permissive.
Please treat any earlier letter from me that said the titles merged in 1983 as corrected by this email. The dates that matter are:
1982/83 — first registration of two titles, without the occupier being heard;
24 July 1986 — first-instance judgment describing one farm while two titles still stood;
2 February 1987 — amalgamation, before the appeal ended;
31 July 1987 — Court of Appeal.
Yours faithfully,


Requester

I do not ask you to adjudicate title. I ask only whether the following instruments exist in your holdings, and for catalogue references, dates, parties, acreages, and whether a plan is attached.

A. The 1877 division
Does the Bute deposit contain a conveyance, agreement, or other instrument of about 1876–1877 by which the Marquess of Bute (or trustees) conveyed or contracted to convey the farmhouse, buildings and about 10 acres adjoining the churchyard at Llandough to Daniel Thomas (or Thomas and another), while retaining about 9 acres of agricultural land to the east?

- is there a plan?
- what acreage is stated?

- a house/buildings holding (Thomas / later Williams), and
- a residual Bute field holding later passed to Western Ground Rents in 1938?

Dear Mr Byrne,

Thank you for your email of 13 October 2026 concerning Freedom of Information request 1264/26.

I provide the clarification and additional search identifiers below. The purpose is to help South Wales Police identify and locate existing recorded information responsive to my original request. I am not seeking to extend the period covered, require the creation of new information, or ask the Force to investigate or determine the underlying property dispute.

For clarity, the requested period remains 1 November to 31 December 1988 inclusive. My request remains for existing, non-personal recorded information only. Personal data is excluded from this FOI request and is being pursued separately through the appropriate subject-access route.

1. Location and alternative site names

The property concerned is Great House Farm, also referred to as Great House and Tŷ Mawr / Ty Mawr, at Llandough-juxta-Penarth in the Vale of Glamorgan, adjoining St Dochdwy’s Church.

The following identifiers may assist searches of occurrence, incident, control-room, deployment or other operational records:

- Site: Great House Farm / Great House / Tŷ Mawr / Ty Mawr.
- Locality: Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Vale of Glamorgan, near Penarth.
- Approximate National Grid Reference: ST 1681 7331; the less precise reference ST 168 733 may also appear.
- Distinctive context: the family farmhouse and associated buildings that were the subject of the possession dispute and were demolished in December 1988.

The locality description is intentional: I refer to Llandough-juxta-Penarth, not the separate Llandough near Cowbridge.

2. Names and organisational identifiers

The principal individual identifier is:

William Beverly Buckler, also referred to in contemporary reporting as William Buckler, Bill Buckler or Billy Buckler.

Relevant corporate or property-related search terms include:

- B.P. Properties Ltd / BP Properties Ltd, the company identified in the property litigation and associated with the demolition.
- BP Pension Trust Ltd and Western Ground Rents Ltd, which appear in the wider historical property context. I include these names only as supplementary indexing terms; I do not assert that either organisation was involved in, or communicated with police about, an event during the requested period.
- Vale of Glamorgan Borough Council and South Glamorgan County Council, the relevant local-government names for the period.
- Court enforcement personnel, bailiffs and any public authority or official recorded as contacting, corresponding with, or requesting assistance from the police in relation to the property.

The following case identifiers may also be useful if records were indexed by litigation or proceedings rather than by address:

- B.P. Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2.
- Buckler v United Kingdom, European Commission of Human Rights application 14464/88, registered on 12 December 1988.

These case identifiers are offered to assist retrieval, not as an assertion that the Force necessarily held records under either reference.

I am supplying names and case references as historical search identifiers. I am not asking for personal data about living individuals. Where a responsive record contains personal data, please consider whether non-personal information can be disclosed separately or after appropriate redaction.

3. Chronology and specific search leads

The following events provide context for identifying any corresponding police records. They are search leads drawn from historical reporting, the heritage record and the family archive; they should not be treated as proof of police involvement.

29–30 November 1988 — possession and eviction

The historical chronology records possession on 29 November 1988. A contemporaneous South Wales Echo report dated 30 November, titled “Angry scenes as farmer evicted” and attributed to Peter Bibby, describes the eviction sequence and reports that bailiffs entered the property and that the roof of an outbuilding had already been partly removed. The chronology also associates demolition of outbuildings with 30 November.

There is therefore a date distinction between the recorded possession date and the newspaper’s account of the eviction. I cannot presently reconcile the dates. Please search across both 29 and 30 November, rather than treating either as an exclusive date for the relevant incident.

2–5 December 1988 — court proceedings and proposed access to belongings

Contemporary reporting describes further court proceedings in the days before the farmhouse was demolished, including an arrangement under which access to collect belongings was reportedly permitted subject to conditions and pending a further hearing.

The precise terms and procedural details should be verified from the original records rather than inferred from press summaries. This chronology may nevertheless help identify any police liaison, requests for assistance, public-order concerns or communications concerning access to the premises.

6 December 1988 — demolition

The heritage record identifies 6 December 1988 as the demolition date. The archived historical chronology reports that a demolition team arrived in the early hours and that the farmhouse was demolished that morning.

I emphasise that the reported arrival time is not evidence that police were present at that time. I am asking whether responsive police records exist, not inviting an assumption that an attendance or deployment took place.

9–13 December 1988 — discrepancy requiring verification

A South Wales Echo report dated 10 December 1988 appears to state that William Buckler was released on bail the previous day, which would be 9 December.

Separately, a notebook attributed to William Buckler and retained in the family archive contains an account referring to police having “locked me up for 2 weeks” and to a search involving family antiques and the taking of documents. The entry is a family-held historical account; it is not, by itself, independently verified proof of detention, a search, seizure or the precise dates involved.

If the notebook’s reference to two weeks from 29 November is literal, it would point to a date around 13 December. That does not readily reconcile with the newspaper’s reported release date of 9 December. I do not ask the Force to accept either account in preference to its own records. The discrepancy is a reason to check the relevant dates and any associated records.

Accordingly, please include 29 November to 13 December 1988 when checking for any potentially relevant custody, detention, search, property-seizure, operational or cross-referenced occurrence records, while retaining the original overall FOI period of 1 November to 31 December 1988. I seek only information falling within the original request’s non-personal scope, including any separable non-personal operational information.

4. Earlier event offered solely as an indexing lead

The archived historical chronology also describes a separate incident at Great House Farm on 29 April 1988, involving bailiffs and a police presence during a stand-off. The account attributes to South Wales Police the position that the officers were there to prevent a breach of the peace, rather than to assist bailiffs.

That event is outside the requested period. I am not asking you to disclose records from April 1988 under this request, and I do not suggest that the earlier incident establishes police attendance in November or December. I mention it only in case any occurrence number, location index or related reference appearing in the records from the requested period would be easier to identify against the same property or dispute.

5. Records sought and search categories

With those identifiers in mind, the records sought remain the existing records described in my original request, insofar as they fall within the period and are held by South Wales Police. In particular, please search for responsive:

1. Incident and control-room records: incident or occurrence logs, calls for assistance, control-room entries, dispatch records and associated incident references relating to the site or the events described above.

2. Police attendance and operational records: deployment, duty, operational or event logs recording any police attendance, requested attendance, planned response or recorded decision concerning the site, its occupants, bailiffs, enforcement personnel or demolition activity.

3. Communications and liaison: recorded correspondence, messages, telephone notes or other communications between police and local-authority officers, court or enforcement personnel, the landowner or developer, their representatives, or other public bodies concerning the property or events during the requested period.

4. Requests for police assistance and public-order matters: records concerning requests for assistance, access to or removal from the premises, the enforcement of possession, complaints, reported disorder, obstruction, public-order concerns, or action proposed or taken in connection with the eviction or demolition.

5. Custody, search and property-related records: to the extent that responsive non-personal information is held and falls within the original scope, any operational references or separable non-personal information concerning a possible detention, premises search, or taking or retention of documents or other property during the relevant dates.

6. Records-management information: where a responsive record is no longer held, any existing record-transfer, retention, destruction or disposal entry sufficient to establish whether the record existed and, if recorded, what became of it.

I am not asserting that each category necessarily generated a record. The purpose of the list is to identify the likely record types and help make the search practicable.

If the Force’s systems use different terminology, location codes, occurrence categories or operational record series, please use the equivalent available indexing terms where reasonably possible.

6. Historical reference material

For convenience, the relevant historical chronology and case background are available here:

- Archived Great House Farm Wiki homepage: https://web.archive.org/web/20260927001835/https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/
- Archived demolition chronology: https://web.archive.org/web/20261006042123/https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/demolition-1988/
- B.P. Properties Ltd v Buckler case page: https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/

These pages are provided as contextual aids and sources of possible search terms, not as substitutes for the Force’s own records or as claims that any particular police record exists.

7. Confirmation of scope and statutory timetable

I trust the above supplies the clarification you require to identify and locate the information requested.

Please confirm receipt and whether this clarification is sufficient for the Force to proceed with its searches. Please also confirm the date from which you calculate the applicable 20-working-day response period and the resulting response deadline.

For the avoidance of doubt:

- the date range remains 1 November–31 December 1988 inclusive;
- the request remains confined to existing recorded information;
- personal data remains excluded from this FOI request and is being pursued separately through the appropriate subject-access route;
- the historical accounts and discrepancies above are search leads, not demands that the Force accept disputed facts; and
- I am not asking the Force to reach conclusions about ownership, the validity of court orders, the conduct of any party, or the truth of any allegation.

Thank you for your assistance.

Yours sincerely,

Requester
